items.headline: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will operate as the Panthers' emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Detroit.
items.summary: King will remain the team's No. 3 QB for the fourth straight week to open the 2026 campaign. The rookie will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Bryce Young and backup Kenny Pickett are removed with injuries.

items.headline: Metchie caught three of five targets for 37 yards during the Panthers' 32-26 win over the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Metchie worked with the first-team offense during Week 4 prep while Jalen Coker was nursing a quadriceps injury, and with the latter inactive for Sunday night's game, Metchie ended the contest with third-most targets on the Panthers behind Tetairoa McMillan (16) and tight end Darren Waller (six). Carolina will be on a bye for Week 5 before hitting the road for Week 6 against Philadelphia on Sunday, Oct. 18. That gives Coker more time to recover from his quad injury, and if he's cleared to play the Eagles, then Metchie would revert to a rotational role on offense.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Moore off the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
items.summary: With Xavier Legette (knee) missing last Sunday's loss to the Browns, Moore was elevated from the practice squad for his 2026 debut in Week 3. Now that Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is also dinged up, Moore gets a spot on the 53-man roster after playing five offensive snaps and another 13 on special teams against Cleveland.

items.headline: Reed reverted to the Panthers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Reed played 10 of Carolina's 75 offensive snaps in Week 4, and he could not haul in his only target during Sunday's 32-26 win versus the Lions. Whether he's elevated again in Week 6 following the Panthers' bye could depend on the availability of Jalen Coker (quadriceps).

items.headline: Sanders (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
items.summary: A fourth-round selection of the Panthers in the 2024 NFL Draft, Sanders will be a healthy scratch for each of the first three games of the 2026 regular season. There doesn't appear to be a clear path to playing time for the Texas product, unless at least one of Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans, Darren Waller or Feleipe Franks were to be unavailable. Sanders' next opportunity to suit up is Week 4 against the Lions on Sunday, Oct. 4.

items.headline: Tremayne caught two of three passes for 32 yards during Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
items.summary: Tremayne actually led all Panthers wide receivers with 69 offensive snaps, and that extra playing time was largely due to the absence of Jalen Coker (quadriceps). Even with the elevated snap count, Sunday's game was the Tetairoa McMillan show, with the second-year wideout finishing with a 14-192-2 receiving line on 16 targets. After not seeing a target from Bryce Young in the first two games of the season, Tremayne has turned nine targets into 6 catches for 115 yards over the Panthers' last two contests. Carolina is on a bye for Week 5, and Tremayne's role would likely shrink against the Eagles in Week 6 if Coker is cleared to return.

items.headline: Tremble caught all four targets for 12 yards in Sunday night's win over the Lions.
items.summary: Involved in a three-man committee at tight end, Tremble's 38 snaps trailed both Mitchell Evans (46) and Darren Waller (40) at the position. He also ran fewer routes than both. Tremble's 11 grabs this season have produced 82 scoreless yards on 15 targets. He has no fantasy appeal.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Tyus from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
items.summary: The 23-year-old running back made his regular-season NFL debut in Sunday's loss to the Browns, logging 14 snaps on special teams. He returned a pair of kickoffs for 47 yards and will now slot in behind Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon on the backfield depth chart.

items.headline: Head coach Dave Canales said Etienne (ankle) will "for sure" be back following the Panthers' Week 5 bye, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Etienne opened the season on injured reserve and is eligible to return in Week 6 at the earliest. Getting Etienne back would give the Panthers another backfield piece while Jonathon Brooks (abdomen) recovers from core muscle surgery. Etienne will likely see most of his playing time on special teams.

items.headline: The Panthers signed Smith-Marsette to the practice squad Tuesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Smith-Marsette returns to the practice squad shortly after being released Sept. 15. The veteran receiver/returner will provide organizational depth for the Panthers as the season unfolds.

items.headline: Burden caught four of six targets for 63 yards and added an 11-yard rush in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Burden finished second on the team in receiving yards, trailing Rome Odunze by 31. Both of Chicago's touchdowns came on the ground, but Tyson Bagent looked capable under center and threw for 268 yards. If Caleb Williams (hamstring) doesn't return in Week 5 against the Packers, Burden will likely continue to catch passes from Bagent. Burden has topped 60 yards in three of four games to begin his sophomore season, but he has yet to exceed 63 receiving yards in a game after reaching the 100-yard mark twice during his rookie campaign.

items.headline: Johnson rushed four times for 16 yards in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets. He added one catch for seven yards on one target.
items.summary: The Bears thoroughly dominated the Jets in time of possession and ran a whopping 93 offensive plays to New York's 34. Johnson saw 10 snaps on offense, as Kyle Monangai (thumb) and D'Andre Swift, who dealt with a knee injury during the practice week, combined to rush 45 times for 204 yards and two touchdowns. Johnson would be in line for additional work if Monangai needs to miss any game action.

items.headline: Kmet caught both of his targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 23-12 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Kmet played 68 of 93 offensive snaps in a game Chicago thoroughly dominated. The veteran tight end remains behind Colston Loveland on the depth chart, but he still plays a significant amount of snaps most weeks. Kmet just doesn't get too involved in the passing game, as he has four catches for 48 yards and a touchdown on seven targets across four contests this season.

items.headline: Roush caught one of three targets for nine yards during the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: The rookie third-rounder did not record a target in the Bears' Week 1 win over the Panthers, but Roush hauled in a nine-yard pass from Caleb Williams (hamstring) late in the third quarter for the former's first NFL catch. Roush is firmly behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet on the depth chart, although those three tight ends, along with the other Bears pass catchers, will all see their scoring floors lowered if Case Keenum is the starting quarterback against the Eagles in Week 3 if Williams and Tyson Bagent (concussion) are both unable to play.

items.headline: All notched two receptions (on three targets) for five yards during Sunday's 20-6 win versus the Texans.
items.summary: All logged 25 offensive snaps in Week 2, finishing behind Drew Sample (36) and Mike Gesicki (21). After not garnering any attention from Joe Burrow in the 33-27 win over the Buccaneers in Week 1, the 26-year-old was targeted three times versus the Texans. All finished his rookie 2024 campaign with 20 receptions for 158 yards, but he didn't play in 2025 due to a knee injury. While All should have a weekly presence in the offense as long as he's healthy, he won't carry much fantasy value as long as Gesicki, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown are available.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Hudson off the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the Bengals' first three games of the regular season, accumulating three catches on as many targets for 17 yards. He'll now be a part of the team's 53-man roster moving forward and will contribute mostly on special teams and in a depth role on offense behind fellow tight ends Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All.

items.headline: Meyers brought in seven of nine targets for 82 yards, returned six kickoffs for 161 yards and ran back two punts for nine yards in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
items.summary: Meyers opened the game as the Bengals' No. 3 receiver, but the former CFL standout was operating as Joe Burrow's top wideout by the time the team's final drive of the afternoon rolled around. Ja'Marr Chase exited the game due to a concussion in the first half, while Tee Higgins was forced from the contest just after the six-minute mark of the fourth quarter due to an adductor injury. Meyers ultimately finished with new career highs across his receiving line while also remaining effective in his special-teams role. With the status of both Chase and Higgins highly uncertain in the immediate aftermath of Sunday's loss and Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) still out of action, Meyers could remain in the No. 1 receiver role in a Week 5 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

items.headline: Perine rushed three times for seven yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Chase Brown carried the ball nine times for just 10 yards, and the Bengals rushed 15 times for just 23 yards as a team, with Joe Burrow scoring a rushing touchdown. Perine has rushed 13 times for 42 yards (3.2 YPC) through four games. He would need an injury to Brown to gain any fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Sample notched zero targets during Sunday's 20-6 victory over the Texans.
items.summary: Sample logged 36 snaps on offense in the win over Houston, finishing ahead of Erick All (25) and Mike Gesicki (21). However, after catching three passes in the 33-27 victory over the Buccaneers in Week 1, he wasn't targeted in Week 2. The 30-year-old veteran has spent his entire career with the Bengals since entering the NFL in 2019, most recently finishing the 2025 campaign with 15 catches (20 targets) for 106 yards and one touchdown. While Sample could find the end zone at some point this season, he's not expected to play a pivotal role on the receiving end. That likely won't change even if Gesicki or All aren't available, considering Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown should continue doing most of the heavy lifting on offense.

items.headline: Young (knee) is not expected to play in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Young suffered a left knee injury in the first quarter of Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Steelers, and he was forced to miss the remainder of the contest. Head coach Zac Taylor provided an update Monday, explaining the wide receiver isn't dealing with a long-term injury, but he will be sidelined for at least one game. The Bengals are expected reevaluate the injury after Week 4 and then determine the next steps for Young.

items.headline: Concepcion secured five of eight targets for 64 yards and returned two punts for 10 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
items.summary: Concepcion and fellow rookie Denzel Boston continued to spark the Browns' air attack Thursday, and the former finished second in receptions and receiving yards while setting the pace in targets. Concepcion's catch and yardage totals also qualified as new career highs, and the productive night served as a welcome bounce-back effort after the rookie first-round pick had been held to 2-9-0 receiving line in the Week 3 win over the Panthers. He should continue to garner plenty of Deshaun Watson's attention in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Fannin secured three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
items.summary: After surging over the last pair of contests, Fannin had a quiet night somewhat reminiscent of his Week 1 performance against the Jaguars. However, the second-year tight end still rewarded fantasy managers by crossing the goal line for the third time in the last two games on a two-yard catch late in the first half. Fannin does have at least five targets in three straight games, and he should have a good chance of continuing to serve as a key target for a resurgent Deshaun Watson in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Steelers, though he will serve as the Browns' emergency quarterback.
items.summary: Green will be inactive for the fourth consecutive game but is listed as Cleveland's QB3. That means Green won't be on the field unless Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Jeudy caught all three of his targets for 36 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over Pittsburgh.
items.summary: It looked like Jeudy could be shut out for the third straight game after finishing the first half with no targets. However, the veteran wideout gave Cleveland a first down with a nine-yard reception late in the third quarter, then came up with two big catches -- a 17-yarder and a 10-yarder -- after the two-minute warning in the fourth to help set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. The two fourth-quarter catches alone accounted for more yardage than Jeudy had recorded across his first three games of the campaign, so perhaps he and QB Deshaun Watson have found some chemistry that they can carry over into a Week 5 matchup versus the Jets.

items.headline: Judkins rushed 17 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in six of seven targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
items.summary: Judkins was in his customary workhorse role in the Browns' ground attack, although as his final rushing line indicates, he found running room hard to come by on most of his carries. Even the second-year back's first rushing touchdown of the season didn't come easy, as Judkins had to power his way in from two yards out in the second quarter. However, he was able to find plenty of success as a receiver, finishing as the team leader in receptions and tying for runner-up status in targets with numbers that also qualified as new career-high figures. Judkins' backfield mates Raheim Sanders and Jaleel McLaughlin combined for just three carries between them -- although the latter took his one tote for a 28-yard touchdown -- so Cleveland's clear lead back will continue to helm the run game in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: McLaughlin turned his lone carry into a 28-yard touchdown during the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
items.summary: McLaughlin was on the field for only one offensive snap Thursday. He made that play count, with the fourth-year pro taking advantage of strong run blocking to reach the end zone for the fourth touchdown of his NFL career. That score may have earned McLaughlin some more reps moving forward, though he's still firmly behind both Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders in the pecking order for backfield snaps. The Browns will hit the road for a Week 5 tilt against the Jets.

items.headline: Sanders accrued two rushes for nine yards and gathered in both of his two targets for seven yards during Thursday's 27-24 win versus the Steelers.
items.summary: Sanders logged 22 offensive snaps, his second-highest mark of the 2026 campaign. However, the 24-year-old was a non-factor offensively. Instead, it was Jaleel McLaughlin who took advantage of his limited workload by scoring a 28-yard rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. While Sanders should remain the No. 2 back on the depth chart behind Quinshon Judkins, assuming the latter stays healthy, he will be difficult to trust from a fantasy standpoint moving ahead.

items.headline: Wallace (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Steelers.
items.summary: A knee injury prevented Wallace from practicing all week, so the sixth-year pro will observe Thursday's game from the sidelines, which means Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley are both in line to see a slight uptick in offensive snaps. Wallace's next opportunity to play is Week 5 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Whiteheart caught one of his two targets for a 17-yard touchdown in Sunday's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Whiteheart played 27 of the Browns' 58 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest, and his one catch, which came with 3:51 remaining, erased a 19-16 deficit and proved to be the difference in the game. The tight end also contributed on 15 special-teams snaps. Whiteheart is the second option at tight end behind Harold Fannin but plays a significant run-blocking role.

items.headline: The Browns signed FitzPatrick to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: FitzPatrick was cleared to resume football activities Sept. 19, completing his recovery from the Achilles tear he suffered in the Packers' Week 16 loss to the Bears last season. FitzPatrick recorded 12 receptions for 72 yards and a touchdown over 15 regular-season games with the Packers in 2025 and will begin his stint in Cleveland serving as organizational depth at tight end.

items.headline: Brown (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie has yet to make his regular-season debut despite making the Cowboys' 53-man roster after a strong training camp, and his next opportunity to do so is Thursday against the Buccaneers. The Cowboys will have five active wide receivers for Sunday's game, with the position group led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

items.headline: Demercado (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.summary: Demercado will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive week, which leaves Tyler Goodson as the lone backup option to Javonte Williams. Demercado's next chance to play is Thursday against the Buccaneers, although he doesn't have a clear path to playing time unless one or both of Williams and Goodson were to miss time.

items.headline: Ferguson caught three of four targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Ferguson is averaging a career-low 2.5 yards after catch per reception and just 0.71 yards per route run through four games to begin the season. He has three touchdowns on the year but otherwise has caught just 12 passes for 83 yards on 15 targets in Dallas' high-volume passing attack. He's merely fighting for scraps behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and has devolved into a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.headline: Flournoy caught four of five targets for 37 yards in Dallas' 34-30 win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.summary: His five targets were actually tied for second on the team, but it was a distant second behind CeeDee Lamb's 21 on Dak Prescott's 45 attempts. Flournoy continues to run plenty of routes as Dallas' top slot receiver between Lamb and George Pickens, but with that duo accounting for most of the receiving production in any given week, Flournoy would likely need an injury to become usable in fantasy.

items.headline: Goodson is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: Todd Archer of ESPN.com initially reported that Goodson would be a healthy scratch. Instead, it will be Emari Demercado (coach's decision) that will be inactive, with Goodson and Javonte Williams the active running backs for the Cowboys in Brazil.

items.headline: Adkins caught all three of his targets for 32 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for six yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
items.summary: Adkins played 23 of the Broncos' 62 offensive snaps while also contributing six snaps to the special-teams unit. The No. 3 tight end was particularly reliable in his complementary role, catching everything thrown his way and scoring a fourth-quarter touchdown to tie the game at 13 points.

items.headline: Badie carried twice for seven yards, caught both of his targets for 32 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and returned one kickoff for 21 yards in a loss to San Francisco in Week 4.
items.summary: Badie chipped in for the Broncos in multiple facets. The highlights of his performance were a 25-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter and a two-point conversion on a run up the middle in the fourth quarter. Badie doesn't have much fantasy value given the low volume of touches he gets on a weekly basis, so it would likely take injuries ahead of him on the RB depth chart for Badie to become an intriguing waiver-wire addition.

items.headline: Bentley (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
items.summary: The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to suit up for a regular-season game. His next chance to do so is Week 5 against the Chargers on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: The Broncos are confident that Bryant avoided a long-term right ankle injury after an MRI on Monday yielded good news, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: The report doesn't offer any specifics regarding what the MRI revealed, but Bryant may have avoided a dreaded high-ankle sprain after exiting Sunday's 24-14 loss to the 49ers. Bryant still appears likely to miss time due to the injury, with Adam Schefter of ESPN relaying Monday that the second-year wideout is expected to be sidelined for "a few weeks." Assuming Bryant is out for at least this Sunday's game against the Chargers, the Broncos would have more reps available for Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin behind starting receivers Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.

items.headline: Engram caught one of five targets for six yards during Sunday's 24-14 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: Engram was held to one or zero receptions for the third straight game, but his five targets matched his season high through four contests. The tight end has produced a meager 66 receiving yards and one touchdown on six catches over 13 targets so far in 2026, making him an especially unattractive fantasy asset.

items.headline: Franklin caught one of two targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
items.summary: With Marvin Mims (foot) inactive, Franklin played 13 of 62 offensive snaps as the clear No. 4 receiver behind Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant and Jaylen Waddle. Franklin's 27-yard grab was his lone catch of the season through two weeks. He'll need an injury to obtain any fantasy relevance in redraft formats.

items.headline: Katsis reverted to Denver's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction report.
items.summary: Katsis made his regular-season debut during Sunday's win over the Rams and played exclusively on special teams, returning three punts for 39 yards and four kickoffs for 107 yards. The rookie undrafted free agent is eligible to be elevated two more times this season.

items.headline: Mims (foot) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: Mims has missed the last two games with a foot injury, but his full practice Wednesday puts him track to play Sunday against the 49ers. Mims ran just nine routes in Week 1 against the Chiefs and is likely to remain in a bit role behind Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant at wide receiver.

items.headline: Nix completed 25 of 42 passes for 214 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions while rushing twice for 10 yards in the Broncos' 24-14 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Nix finished with a serviceable passing line, but he averaged only 5.1 yards per attempt and wasn't able to overcome a second-half deficit like he pulled off in Week 3 against the Rams. The third-year signal-caller lost talented second-year wideout Pat Bryant to an ankle injury during the contest, and he found his greatest success when targeting RJ Harvey, who was on the receiving end of 10 of his completions. Nix has just a 60.0 percent completion rate and a modest 25 rushing yards through four games, but he may have a chance to boost those numbers against a winless Chargers team on the road in Week 5.

items.headline: Sutton caught just one of six targets for four yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: Sutton has been wholly unproductive to begin the season, producing just nine catches for 86 scoreless yards on 21 targets through four games. His 0.69 yards per route run is easily a low point for his career. Sutton has not been productive as a fantasy player so far, and it doesn't help that he plays in a low-scoring offense that likes to spread the ball around to multiple different players.

items.headline: Humphrey signed a practice-squad contract with the Broncos on Saturday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
items.summary: Humphrey was released by Denver on Friday but quickly inked a deal to remain in the organization. However, Gabriel notes that the Broncos aren't elevating anyone for Sunday's matchup against San Francisco, so Humphrey won't be active while he resides on the practice squad. The veteran wideout has logged just three offensive snaps so far this season and didn't catch his only target.

items.headline: Conklin (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.summary: Conklin has been used sparingly through the first two games of the regular season, and the veteran tight end will be a healthy scratch Sunday against the team he played for from 2022 to 2024. Brock Wright and Jackson Meeks will provide depth at the position behind Sam LaPorta, and Conklin's next opportunity to play is Week 4 against the Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 4.

items.headline: Goff completed 32 of 52 passes for 412 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
items.summary: The Lions surprisingly found themselves trailing throughout the majority of the second half, leading to Goff putting up season-high totals in all of completions, pass attempts and passing yards. The veteran signal-caller did see a three-game streak of multi-TD-pass tallies come to an end, with Sunday night's sole scoring strike going to Sam LaPorta from eight yards out late in the fourth quarter. Goff connected with seven different targets overall and helped facilitate Jameson Williams' first 100-yard effort of the season, but he'll now be tasked with trying to prevent Detroit from falling below .500 in a Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

items.headline: Williams secured six of eight targets for 102 yards in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
items.summary: Williams led the Lions in receiving yards on the night, and all three components of the fourth-year speedster's receiving line were also season-high figures. The productive performance was an especially welcome sight for fantasy managers who were banking on a true breakout season for Williams after back-to-back 1,000-yard campaigns, and the 2022 first-round pick should have a good opportunity to carry over the momentum into a favorable Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

items.headline: The Lions signed Keys to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Keys has been bouncing around the league for the past three seasons and has yet to appear in an NFL regular-season game. He'll now serve as organizational depth at receiver for Detroit.

items.headline: The Lions signed Kitselman (leg) to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Kitselman reached an injury settlement with the Lions during training camp in mid-August due to a leg injury he sustained in practice. He's since been medically cleared to sign with a team, and he's opted to return to Detroit as a member of the practice squad. Kitselman would be a candidate to be elevated to the active roster if one of the four tight ends on the Lions' 53-man roster were to miss time.

items.headline: Brooks is questionable to return to Sunday's Week 4 matchup against Tampa Bay due to an ankle injury, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Brooks began the game in solid form, rushing four times for 30 yards and catching his lone target for five yards before limping to the sideline near the end of the first quarter. He'll be evaluated by team trainers before a determination is made about whether Brooks will be able to return. In the meantime, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson are Green Bay's two healthy running backs.

items.headline: Judge denies request to seal records in Josh Jacobs case
items.summary: The judge who presided over the criminal case of Packers RB Josh Jacobs denied a request by the victim to have evidence permanently sealed.

items.headline: Johnson logged eight carries for 42 yards and lost one fumble in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.summary: Johnson had a strong 5.3 yards per carry in the win but coughed up the football in a close game. The running back relinquished the ball to Tykee Smith with 9:13 remaining in the fourth quarter on the Tampa Bay 4-yard line while the Packers were up by only three points. The defense held off the Buccaneers' offense, but it appears the Packers chose to ride MarShawn Lloyd to finish out the game.

items.headline: Lloyd rushed seven times for 13 yards and brought in all five targets for 36 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.summary: It was more of the same on the ground for Lloyd, who barely eclipsed the season-low 11 rushing yards he produced in Week 3 against the Falcons. However, the third-year back set new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets, offering some modest fantasy value on the afternoon. Lloyd's backfield mate Kaleb Johnson led the ground attack with eight carries for 42 yards Sunday, and although Lloyd remains largely ineffective as a runner, he'll likely remain in a relevant role in Week 5 at home against the Bears if the ankle injury that forced Chris Brooks' exit from the contest keeps him sidelined for that divisional contest.

items.headline: Melton logged 21 of 66 offensive snaps during Thursday's 35-14 loss to the Falcons but did not catch his only target. He also recorded two tackles and turned two kickoff returns into 46 yards.
items.summary: Melton played a total of 42 snaps Thursday, split evenly between special teams and offense, and his offensive snap count was fourth-most among Packers wide receivers. Despite the spike in playing time, Melton shouldn't factor into the team's offensive game plan unless a larger role opens up for the 2022 seventh-rounder due to the absence of one or multiple wide receivers.

items.headline: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-two yards while also adding 52 kickoff-return yards and 19 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Moore was unable to build off his seven targets from Week 3, garnering his fewest targets since Week 1 in the team's marginal victory versus Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old doesn't carry much upside as a fantasy asset, and he figures to operate as a distant No. 3 option at wide receiver behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden moving forward.

items.headline: Smith caught his only target for 19 yards during Green bay win Sunday versus the Falcons.
items.summary: Smith has now managed to catch a pass in three of his four appearances during the current campaign while serving as the No. 2 tight end behind Tucker Kraft. Smith has hauled in five of his seven targets for 85 yards so far this season.

items.headline: Sturdivant tallied three catches on as many targets for 22 yards during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
items.summary: Sturdivant's nine-yard catch late in the third quarter was the first of his NFL career. He went on to haul in two more passes of three and 10 yards in the fourth quarter and finished Thursday's contest having played 21 of the Packers' 66 snaps on offense (31.8 percent). Most of that playing time came when Green Bay was facing a large deficit, but Sturdivant figures to see at least some involvement in the offense given the uncertainty around the status of Jayden Reed (neck) for the rest of the 2026 season.

items.headline: Watson secured all three targets for 47 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
items.summary: Watson led the Packers in receiving yards on an afternoon when Jordan Love threw for only 197 yards. The speedy wideout's reception, receiving yardage and target totals were all season lows, but Watson has still enjoyed a productive start to the campaign with a 20-331-4 line on 32 targets and good health throughout. Watson and the Packers' air attack as a whole will look for a boost in production at the expense of the division-rival Bears in a Week 5 home matchup next Sunday.

items.headline: The Packers signed Owen to the practice squad Wednesday, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Owen appeared in two regular-season games with the Colts last season, returning five kickoffs for 141 yards and one punt for two yards. He'll provide some wideout depth in Green Bay due to Jayden Reed (neck) and Savion Williams (ankle) being banged up.

items.headline: Bond reverted to the Texans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Bond played nine offensive snaps in the Texans' 19-17 loss to the Colts on Sunday. The wide receiver was unable to reel in his sole target in the contest. Bond has now played 22 offensive snaps and 20 special-teams snaps over two active-roster elevations in 2026.

items.headline: Boutte caught three of four targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
items.summary: With Nico Collins back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury, he dominated targets and left the remainder of the Houston pass catchers fighting for leftovers. Boutte ran 24 routes on C.J. Stroud's 35 dropbacks, but the summer trade pickup has yet to really make an impact with the Texans, recording nine catches for 115 yards on 13 targets after four games.

items.headline: Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 46 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
items.summary: With Nico Collins (hamstring) back from a two-game absence, Hutchinson saw his snaps cut pretty significantly, as he played just 17 of 55 offensive snaps. He still saw five targets, but Hutchinson appears to be the biggest loser at wide receiver with Collins back in action. He can be left on waivers in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Klein (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.summary: The rookie second-rounder will be a healthy scratch for the first time this season, and his next chance to play is Week 5 against the Titans on Sunday, Oct. 11. Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan will serve as the Texans' depth options at tight end behind Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau.

items.headline: Moreau caught both of his targets for 34 yards and added a tackle on special teams during Sunday's 20-6 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Moreau was listed as a starter, though he played only 23 of the Texans' 80 offensive plays, well behind Dalton Schultz's 54 snaps. Moreau ended up fourth on the Texans in receiving yards, which included a 25-yard catch early in the second quarter, and he's up to a 4-49-0 receiving line through two regular-season games. The Texans hit the road for Week 3 against the Colts, and while Moreau will contribute on offense and special teams, his pass-catching production will be limited while working behind Schultz.

items.headline: Noel caught all three targets for 85 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys. He added four rushing yards on one attempt.
items.summary: Despite Nico Collins (hamstring) returning to the lineup after missing two games, Noel remained a big part of the offense, as Xavier Hutchinson was the big loser in terms of snaps and routes. Noel ran just one fewer route than Kayshon Boutte and six fewer than Collins. Through four games, Noel has nine catches for 186 yards on 12 targets. He has a chance to become the Texans' WR2 behind Collins at some point this season, especially if Boutte doesn't start producing.

items.headline: The Texans signed Ogunbowale off the Raiders' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Ogunbowale signed with the Raiders' practice squad after being trimmed from the team's roster during final cuts. The running back now returns to Houston, where he participated in 129 offensive snaps and 281 special-teams snaps over 17 regular-season games in 2025.

items.headline: Wayne caught two of his seven targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 20-6 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Wayne garnered plenty of C.J. Stroud's attention due to the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring) in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver saw the third-most targets for the Texans behind Dalton Schultz and Xavier Hutchinson, but he wasn't efficient with them while playing on 40 of the team's 80 offensive snaps in the contest.

items.headline: Brooks (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Friday.
items.summary: Brooks will miss at least four games. However, the 26-year-old has seen action only on special teams during the 2026 campaign, so his extended absence won't impact the usual day-to-day operations for the Texans offense.

items.headline: Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that he expects the Texans to open Dell's (knee) 21-day practice window this week, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.summary: Still on the mend from the severe multi-ligament knee injury that he sustained Dec. 21, 2024, Dell was able to take part in some full-contact practices during training camp but sat out the Texans' entire preseason slate before he was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return prior to Week 1. The 26-year-old wideout appears to have responded well to the extra recovery time to begin the regular season, and he could be ready to mix into drills when Houston kicks off Week 5 prep Wednesday. Dell likely won't be activated ahead of Sunday's contest in Tennessee, but the Texans' willingness to open his practice window suggests that he's expected to be ready for game action by midseason.

items.headline: Graham Mertz shares his excitement for No. 21 Ole Miss vs. No. 4 Florida
items.summary: Houston Texans quarterback and Gators alum Mertz joins The Paul Finebaum Show and discusses how he's ready to see Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels go against Aaron Philo and Florida.

items.headline: Houston cut Oliver from its practice squad Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Less than two weeks after signing Oliver to their practice squad, the Texans are now parting ways with him. Over three regular-season games with the Titans in 2025, he caught his only target for eight yards.

items.headline: The Texans signed Saunders to their practice squad Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Saunders is returning to Houston, where he spent time this offseason after signing with the team as an undrafted free agent in May. With Nico Collins still battling a hamstring injury, Saunders could provide additional depth at receiver if Collins is forced to continue missing time.

items.headline: The Texans placed Whittington (quadriceps) on the practice-squad injured list Thursday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.summary: Whittington suffered a torn quad during practice this week, and while the move to the injured list will prevent him from being eligible for elevation for four weeks, the rookie could be sidelined for longer. Whittington linked up with Houston as an undrafted free agent in early May following a strong senior season with Oregon.

items.headline: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London.
items.summary: Alie-Cox missed the Colts' first two practices of the week due to an illness, but he returned to the field Friday and avoided a designation heading into the weekend. He'll be ready to serve in his usual depth role at tight end behind starter Tyler Warren.

items.headline: Dulin (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London.
items.summary: Though he had been listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Dulin had always appeared likely to put an end to his two-game absence after practicing fully Thursday and Friday. Dulin projects to make his biggest impact on special teams when the Colts are at full strength at receiver, but he'll be needed to handle a depth role on offense Week 4 while fellow wideouts Keenan Allen (groin) and Darius Slayton (coach's decision) are inactive.

items.headline: Giddens (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans.
items.summary: Giddens was a full participant in practice after being unavailable for Week 2 against the Chiefs due to a knee injury. He'll be a healthy scratch for Sunday's AFC South showdown, with Seth McGowan being the lone depth option out of the backfield behind bell-cow running back Jonathan Taylor. Giddens' next opportunity to play is Week 4 against the Commanders on Sunday, Oct. 4.

items.headline: The Colts signed Gould from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: Gould was elevated to the active roster for the Colts' Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs. The wide receiver played nine special-teams snaps in the loss, not touching the field for the offense. Now a member of the active roster, Gould will likely continue in his role as a special-teamer due to the absence of Ashton Dulin (ankle).

items.headline: Leonard is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London as the Colts' emergency No. 3 quarterback.
items.summary: Leonard hasn't been active for any of the Colts' first four games after Anthony Richardson beat him out for the No. 2 job coming out of the preseason. The second-year player out of Notre Dame will only be available in the event both starter Daniel Jones and Richardson are unable to finish the game.

items.headline: McGowan turned six carries into 31 yards and caught one of two targets for seven yards during Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders in London. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
items.summary: McGowan actually saw most of his offensive output in the second quarter with four carries for 18 yards and his seven-yard catch. Most of his on-field production figures to come on special teams as a returner, but the rookie seventh-rounder would be thrust into RB1 duties if Jonathan Taylor were to miss time. The Colts will hit the road for Week 5 against the Steelers this Sunday.

items.headline: Richardson is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London.
items.summary: Richardson has yet to take any snaps this season, but he'll suit up for a fourth straight game as Daniel Jones' backup after securing the No. 2 job coming out of the preseason. Meanwhile, second-year player Riley Leonard will be inactive as the Colts' emergency No. 3 quarterback.

items.headline: Slayton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London.
items.summary: Even though the Colts' depth at wide receiver will be tested in Week 4 with Keenan Allen (groin) inactive and Alec Pierce (heel) out for a second straight game while on injured reserve, Slayton apparently needs more time to get acclimated after signing with Indianapolis on Sept. 21. With Slayton being a healthy scratch, the Colts will proceed with Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Deion Burks, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Anthony Gould as their available options at wideout.

items.headline: Treadwell caught five of six targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders.
items.summary: With Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve and Keenan Allen (groin) inactive for Week 4, Treadwell paced the Colts' wideouts with 56 offensive snaps and ran a team-high 36 routes on Daniel Jones' 37 dropbacks. Josh Downs and Ashton Dulin fell in line behind Treadwell in terms of playing time at the position. He has nine catches for 123 yards on 11 targets through four games.

items.headline: Westbrook-Ikhine reverted to the practice squad with Indianapolis on Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Westbrook-Ikhine was elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders. The wide receiver failed to record any stats while playing 11 snaps on offense, and he added one tackle on kick coverage while logging 13 snaps with the special-teams unit. With Keenan Allen (groin) not 100 percent, it's possible that Westbrook-Ikhine is elevated again for the team's Week 5 matchup with Pittsburgh.

items.headline: The Colts signed Pancol to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Pancol participated in the Colts' training camp this summer but was waived by the team on Aug. 30. While the signing is a step in the right direction for Pancol's NFL career, he might not get an opportunity to appear in a regular-season game for Indianapolis anytime soon. The wideout appeared in 57 games for Duke from 2019-2024, amassing 130 catches for 1,710 yards and 14 touchdowns, adding 40 yards and two scores off seven carries.

items.headline: Abdullah carried the ball three times for 11 yards and caught his only target for two yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The 30-year-old was most involved on special teams and saw just six of the Jaguars' 59 offensive snaps, finishing behind Bhayshul Tuten (30), Chris Rodriguez (13) and LeQuint Allen (nine) in the backfield. Abdullah should continue to see a similar workload as long as the RBs ahead of him on the depth chart remain healthy.

items.headline: Allen (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Bills.
items.summary: Allen was limited by a lingering hip injury in all three practices during Week 4 prep, but the second-year pro has been given the green light to play Sunday. He's seen little action offense as the RB3 behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, with Allen securing two catches (on three targets) for nine yards while not logging a carry through three regular-season games.

items.headline: Boerkircher (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Thursday's game against the Bengals.
items.summary: Boerkircher was held out of Thursday's practice due to an illness, but he's past his ailment and will be available to play Sunday. The rookie second-rounder has one catch (on two targets) for nine yards through three regular-season games while serving as the Jaguars' TE2 behind Brenton Strange.

items.headline: Cameron hauled in both of his targets for 42 yards during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 45 yards.
items.summary: Cameron got on the board in the second quarter with a 29-yard catch before connecting with Trevor Lawrence on a 13-yard pass in the third. The rookie sixth-rounder played 22 of the Jaguars' 61 offensive snaps (36.1 percent), fourth-most among Jacksonville's wide receivers. Cameron has a 5-74-2 receiving line on six targets through four games, and his scoring floor figures to remain limited unless the Jaguars are without one or more of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas or Jakobi Meyers. Up next for the Jaguars is a Week 5 home game against the Eagles.

items.headline: Ewers is set to be the backup quarterback for the Jaguars in Sunday's game against the Patriots, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
items.summary: With quarterback Nick Mullens not receiving a practice squad elevation, Ewers is set to be the backup in Week 3. The quarterback was a healthy scratch for the first two games of the 2026 season as the Jaguars utilized Mullens as the primary backup to Trevor Lawrence, but the 23-year-old Ewers will now serve in the role the team traded for him to fill.

items.headline: Meyers caught three of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 22-17 win against the Bengals.
items.summary: Meyers finished second on the team in targets behind tight end Brenton Strange (eight), but his performance was far from noteworthy. The wide receiver has operated as a distant No. 2 option behind Parker Washington at his position this season, and Sunday's performance was his third game with 40 or fewer receiving yards over four contests.

items.headline: Strange caught seven of eight targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
items.summary: Cincinnati annually plays bad defense against opposing tight ends, and Strange was able to take advantage of the clean matchup by leading the team in targets, catches and receiving yards Sunday. An every-down tight end in Jacksonville's potent offense, he's a weekly fringe TE1/2 headed into next Sunday's game against the Eagles. On the season, Strange has 14 catches for 167 yards and one touchdown on 18 targets.

items.headline: Washington secured one of three targets for seven yards, rushed once for three yards and returned one punt for three yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
items.summary: Washington had been Trevor Lawrence's top target by a comfortable margin over the first three games of the season, but the Bengals effectively shut down the bulk of Jacksonville's wide-receiver production Sunday. Washington saw the biggest downturn, making it a forgettable fantasy afternoon overall despite the team-level success the Jaguars enjoyed. Washington figures to have an uphill battle in terms of a potential Week 5 resurgence as well, considering the Jaguars will face off with a talented Eagles defense in a Week 5 matchup in London next Sunday.

items.headline: Williams (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
items.summary: Williams will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive week, and the rookie sixth-rounder's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Bengals on Sunday, Oct. 4. The Jaguars will go with five active wide receivers in Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, Jakobi Meyers, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Bates to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Bates joins the Jaguars after reaching an injury settlement with the Browns in late August and receiving medical clearance Monday. Bates played in nine 2025 regular-season games between Cleveland and the Texans, logging four receptions (on five targets) for 48 yards.

items.headline: Allen failed to reel in his only target in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Allen went without a reception for the fourth straight contest to open his NFL career. The wide receiver impressed during the preseason, but he has yet to make his mark during the regular season. Allen could be set for an expanded role following the team's Week 5 bye week though, as both Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) suffered injuries against Las Vegas, the latter of which is season-ending.

items.headline: Gray caught two of his three targets for 17 yards in the Chiefs' 30-27 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Gray was utilized at a similar rate to No. 1 tight end Travis Kelce in the contest. The tight end once again contributed to blocking for Kenneth Walker in 12-personnel packages but has not logged a lot of attention in the Chiefs' passing offense.

items.headline: Johnson caught his lone target for 10 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: The rookie running back didn't handle a single rushing attempt behind Kenneth Walker's 22 carries for 177 yards and two touchdowns. Johnson still played 17 offensive snaps and remains the clear backup and bench stash to own in fantasy should something ever happen to Walker.

items.headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Nussmeier will once again be the Chiefs' emergency QB3, meaning the rookie seventh-rounder is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Royals caught both of his targets for six yards and a touchdown while logging two tackles on kick coverage in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Colts.
items.summary: Royals made an impact on his 12 offensive snaps and seven special-teams snaps. The wide receiver scored the Chiefs' last touchdown of the game midway through the third quarter on a 1-yard pass. The fourth-round rookie may see an uptick in usage if coach Andy Reid finds new ways to use the speedy young player as the season develops.

items.headline: Wiley (coach's decision) is inactive against the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Wiley will once again be a healthy scratch, and his next chance to make his 2026 regular-season debut is Week 6 against the Chargers on Oct. 18. The Chiefs will go with Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool as the active tight ends for Sunday's AFC West showdown.

items.headline: Worthy caught four of seven targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Worthy finished second on the team in targets and receiving yards behind Tyquan Thornton, who caught five of eight targets for 111 yards and two touchdowns prior to suffering an ankle injury in the fourth quarter. Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited the game in the first quarter, so Worthy is the top healthy wide receiver for Kansas City, though Rice will have a chance to heal during the Week 5 bye before the Chargers come to town in Week 6.

items.headline: Jeanty rushed 15 times for 58 yards while catching six of eight targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Jeanty posted another inefficient performance on the ground, as he's averaging just 3.4 yards per carry this season and has yet to score on 78 rushing attempts. The workhorse running back has made up for his pedestrian performance on the ground by contributing consistently through the air, as Jeanty has 19 catches for 155 yards and two receiving TDs heading into the Raiders' Week 5 road game against the Patriots. Backup Mike Washington had just 17 yards on 10 touches Sunday, so he isn't making much of a case to cut further into Jeanty's hefty workload.

items.headline: Mayer caught eight of 10 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Mayer led the Raiders in catches while finishing four receiving yards and one target shy of Brock Bowers' team-high totals. Kirk Cousins has relied heavily on his tight ends in the passing game, and even third-stringer Ian Thomas got in on the fun with a 27-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter. Bowers will continue to lead the position group in Week 5 against the Patriots, but Mayer remains an integral part of Vegas' offense as well.

items.headline: Mendoza did not see the field for the Raiders' 30-27 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
items.summary: Mendoza spent all of Sunday's game on the sidelines while Kirk Cousins took every snap under center, with the veteran quarterback completing 31 of 52 passes for 365 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. Even with the loss, the Raiders are off to a 3-1 start to the season, so Mendoza is unlikely to see playing time unless Cousins were to miss time or Las Vegas' 2026 campaign takes a turn for the worse.

items.headline: Nailor (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Chiefs.
items.summary: Nailor took a blow to the head late in the second quarter, and he was ultimately diagnosed with a concussion. The wide receiver will finish his day having recorded no stats. In his absence, Tre Tucker, Cody White and Dareke Young will operate as the Raiders' top options at wide receiver.

items.headline: O'Connell (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Raiders' emergency third quarterback against the Chiefs on Sunday.
items.summary: As the emergency QB3, O'Connell is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Tucker's eight targets tied Ashton Jeanty for third on the team behind Brock Bowers' 11 and Michael Mayer's 10 on a day Kirk Cousins attempted 52 passes. With Bowers back from a knee injury, Tucker has turned 12 targets into eight catches for 87 yards over the last two weeks with Bowers in the lineup. He's a big-play threat is a boom-or-bust, low-floor fantasy bet most weeks.

items.headline: Washington rushed nine times for 18 yards in Sunday's 30-27 loss to the Chiefs. He added one catch for minus-1 yard on two targets.
items.summary: Washington's nine carries were his most in a single game to begin the season and came one week after he broke out for 54 yards and a touchdown on five carries against the Saints. The rookie running back closed the gap some on Ashton Jeanty atop the backfield, but Washington didn't do much with his chances against Kansas City. He remains one of the stronger fantasy bench stashes.

items.headline: White caught two of four targets for 36 yards during Sunday's 30-27 loss to Kansas City.
items.summary: White failed to make it three games in a row with a touchdown, but his 36 receiving yards and four targets were new season highs for the wideout. The 27-year-old has now caught five of 10 targets for 64 yards and three touchdowns over four contests to open the 2026 campaign. White was already slotted in as the team's No. 3 wide receiver with Jack Bech (forearm) on injured reserve, but he could operate in an even more prominent role Week 5 against New England after No. 2 option Jalen Nailor suffered a concussion Sunday.

items.headline: Young (hamstring) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
items.summary: The wide receiver exited Sunday's win over the Chargers during the second half and opened the practice week with a limited session Wednesday. Young should be on track to play Sunday at New Orleans now that he's back, but his role will likely remain split between special teams and offense, areas where he's logged respective snap counts of 31 and 22 thus far this season.

items.headline: The Raiders placed Bech (forearm) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: Bech will be sidelined for at least the Raiders' next four games after sustaining a fractured left forearm during Sunday's 35-27 win over the Saints. In a corresponding move, the Raiders signed Cody White off their practice squad. White, who already has three touchdowns this season, is the leading candidate to replace Bech as the No. 3 wideout behind Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor.

items.headline: Head coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that the hope is that Thornton (undisclosed) will be back at practice ahead of the Raiders' Week 5 road tilt against the Patriots, Levi Edwards of the Raiders' official site reports.
items.summary: Thornton opened the season on injured reserve due to an undisclosed injury that prevented him from participating in the majority of August practices during training camp. Once he's cleared to return, Thornton will likely operate in a depth role at wide receiver behind Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Cody White.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Dorsett to their practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Dorsett is in a familiar position after spending almost all of last season on Las Vegas' practice squad. He received one elevation but ended up being a healthy scratch for that contest. Dorsett has played in parts of eight NFL campaigns but hasn't appeared in a regular-season contest since 2023. He'll likely serve as organizational wideout depth for the Raiders, with a gameday elevation potentially dependent on the health of the team's WRs on the active roster.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Scott to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Rams waived Scott on Aug. 30. The wide receiver cleared waivers and remained a free agent until Monday. Scott last played in the regular season in 2024, logging one target over 20 offensive snaps across 11 games with the Bears.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Wright to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Wright takes the spot vacated by Dare Ogunbowale, who signed to Houston's 53-man roster Tuesday. Wright appeared in three games with the Bucs last season, rushing three times for six yards on extremely limited opportunities.

items.headline: Gadsden secured five of eight targets for 36 yards and recorded a two-yard carry during Sunday's 30-23 defeat in Seattle.
items.summary: With position mates David Njoku (fibula) on IR and Charlie Kolar (forearm) sidelined the last two contests, Gadsden has had uneven results, posting a bagel on three targets in Week 3 at Buffalo before Sunday's season-best performance. Gadsden likely was helped this week by the early exit of No. 1 WR Ladd McConkey (foot), but the former's efficiency (9.5 YPC, 5.7 YPT) has been lacking in a floundering Chargers offense so far this season. In any case, for as long as Njoku and Kolar are out of the lineup, Gadsden shouldn't have a problem leading the team's TEs in most receiving categories.

items.headline: Harris caught three of five targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Harris led the team in receiving yards for the second straight week, recording at least 53 receiving yards for the third contest in a row. Ladd McConkey (foot) aggravated his pre-existing foot injury in the contest, and he is considered week-to-week for the time being. If McConkey is unavailable in Week 5 versus the Broncos, Harris may have a chance to operate as the team's primary pass-catcher.

items.headline: Herbert reverted to the Chargers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Herbert played four of the Chargers' 71 offensive snaps during Sunday's 30-23 loss at Seattle, and he added 14 snaps on special teams. He can be elevated once more this season before the Chargers would have to sign him to their 53-man roster to make him eligible to suit up.

items.headline: Johnston caught one of two targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks. He added one carry for minus-4 yards.
items.summary: Despite Ladd McConkey (foot) playing just 24 of 71 offensive snaps, including zero in the second half, Johnston was a ghost most of the afternoon before hauling in a deep ball in the fourth quarter. Johnston continues to pace the team in snaps and routes at wide receiver, but he has little to show for it this season, posting just seven catches for 108 yards and no touchdowns on 19 targets. Johnston won't be a recommended fantasy play next Sunday against the Broncos, even if Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) are still banged up.

items.headline: Lance (groin) is active for Sunday's game against Seattle.
items.summary: Lance was listed as questionable but will shed the tag and suit up in Week 4. With Lance cleared to play, DJ Uiagalelei is inactive, though he will serve as the team's emergency signal-caller if necessary.

items.headline: Mitchell tallied 10 carries for 39 yards and five catches (on six targets) for 24 yards during Sunday's 30-23 defeat at Seattle.
items.summary: Mitchell surprisingly led the Chargers backfield in touches with 15, ahead of Omarion Hampton's 11 and Kimani Vidal's seven, but unlike his position mates he didn't reach the end zone. Because Mitchell's touch count has increased in each successive week this season, he's trending in a positive direction, but until one of the trio is handling most of the RB reps, it'll be difficult to trust any of them for fantasy purposes on a weekly basis. He next takes the field next Sunday against the Broncos.

items.headline: The Chargers signed Rucci off the Jaguars' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: With both Charlie Kolar (forearm) and David Njoku (fibula) slated to go on injured reserve, the Chargers needed more depth at tight end behind second-year pro Oronde Gadsden. Rucci did not record a catch across four regular-season games with the Vikings in 2025, and he figures to serve mostly as a blocker on offense and a contributor on special teams, with Gadsden being the pass-catching tight end for Justin Herbert.

items.headline: Thompson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
items.summary: Thompson will miss a second consecutive game while working through a quadriceps injury. He was unable to practice during Week 4 prep, so a limited session ahead of Week 5 against the Broncos would indicate that the rookie fourth-rounder is progressing in his recovery. Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will both work in rotational roles behind Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris in Thompson's absence.

items.headline: Uiagalelei (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus Seattle, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
items.summary: Trey Lance (groin) is available to suit up in Week 4, meaning Uiagalelei will be a healthy scratch. However, if Lance and Justin Herbert exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection, Uiagalelei will serve as the team's emergency signal-caller.

items.headline: Valdes-Scantling was signed to the Chargers' active roster Wednesday.
items.summary: Valdes-Scantling inked a deal to join the practice squad with Los Angeles on Sept. 15, and he will now get a shot with the active roster. The 31-year-old will provide the team with another veteran option at wide receiver ahead of Week 3 versus the Bills.

items.headline: The Chargers placed Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve Wednesday.
items.summary: Njoku will be sidelined for at least the Chargers' next four games after sustaining a fibula injury in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) was able to avoid placement on IR but has already been ruled out for the Chargers' Week 3 contest in Buffalo, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the top option on the depth chart heading into that game.

items.headline: The Chargers signed Jennings to the practice squad Thursday.
items.summary: Jennings was recently cut by the Chargers but will now find his way back to the team, albeit as a member of the practice squad. It's unknown if the 29-year-old will see some regular-season snaps for Los Angeles moving forward, though it may take an injury or two for that to happen. Even then, Jennings isn't expected to have much of a role on offense. In a corresponding move, the Bolts released long snapper Spencer Triplett from the practice squad.

items.headline: Allen caught his only target for seven yards in Monday night's win over the Giants.
items.summary: The tight end played 52 percent of the offensive snaps, trailing both Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson at the position on a night the Rams again used a heavy dose of tight ends with Puka Nacua (hip) inactive. Allen would need an injury ahead of him to enter the conversation for fantasy.

items.headline: Atwell caught one of two targets for 19 yards during Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants.
items.summary: Atwell remained an afterthought in the offense, even with Puka Nacua (hip) unavailable, and only played 11 of the team's 62 offensive snaps. He ranked behind Konata Mumpfield (43), Davante Adams (40) and Xavier Smith (26) at wide receiver in offensive snaps, and even if Nacua remains inactive for a Week 3 tilt versus Denver, Atwell will have limited appeal.

items.headline: The Rams signed Bachman from their practice squad to their 53-man roster Saturday.
items.summary: Bachman spent a portion of training camp with the Rams before signing to the practice squad in early September. He's evidently made a positive impression, as Los Angeles has elected to promote him to the active roster despite the fact that he's yet to see gameday action this season. Bachman will assume the roster spot vacated by tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle), who landed on IR on Friday. However, Bachman doesn't stand to see many opportunities on offense with the Rams currently fielding a relatively healthy wideout corps.

items.headline: The Rams signed Connors from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: Connors was signed to the active roster after fellow running back Ronnie Rivers (calf) was placed on injured reserve last Wednesday. Connors was elevated to the active roster ahead of the Rams' Week 3 loss to the Broncos as the No. 3 running back behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The 23-year-old will continue to fill that role for the team on the 53-man roster in Rivers' absence.

items.headline: Higbee caught five of six targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: Higbee was the Rams' TE1 for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Colby Parkinson (shoulder/knee). Even with superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua back from a two-game absence, Higbee still finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most receiving yards on the Rams, and his six targets were fourth-most behind Kyren Williams (13), Nacua (12) and Davante Adams (nine). After a quiet start to the season, Higbee has a 13-129-1 receiving line on 17 targets over his last two games. Higbee may have shown enough to warrant an established role in the Rams' offense moving forward, even if Parkinson is cleared to return for Week 5 against the Bills.

items.headline: Mumpfield suffered a rotator cuff contusion during Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.summary: Mumpfield briefly exited the game before returning to the field, and head coach Sean McVay and the team don't appear to be overly worried about the injury. With Puka Nacua returning to action Sunday, Mumpfield saw only three targets, reeling in one catch for seven yards in the victory.

items.headline: Parkinson (shoulder/knee) is inactive for Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Eagles.
items.summary: The veteran tight end took a questionable tag into the weekend after missing practice all week, and Parkinson's inactive status has now been confirmed. While he tends to his pair of injuries and targets a return for a Monday night, Oct. 12 home showdown with the Bills in Week 5, Parkinson's snaps and targets are expected to be absorbed by Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and rookie second-round pick Max Klare, the Rams' three remaining healthy tight ends with Terrance Ferguson (ankle, IR) also unavailable.

items.headline: Simpson is inactive and serving as the Rams' emergency third quarterback Sunday versus the Eagles.
items.summary: Simpson has now been inactive as Los Angeles' emergency third QB each of the first four weeks to begin the campaign. He'll be eligible to enter Sunday's contest only if both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett become unavailable due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Whittington (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Whittington wasn't available for Monday's 28-6 win over the Giants. He didn't practice Wednesday to begin the week. However, head coach Sean McVay indicated the wideout would be available in Week 3, so his full participation in Friday's practice and omission from the injury report isn't a surprise. With Puka Nacua (hip) doubtful, Whittington could be in line for a more prominent role alongside Davante Adams.

items.headline: The Rams placed Ferguson (ankle) on injured reserve Friday.
items.summary: Ferguson underwent X-rays on an ankle injury during this past Sunday's loss at Denver, and while he was able to return to the contest, he then didn't practice in any capacity Wednesday through Friday before being ruled out for Week 4 action. With Ferguson out for at least the next four games and Colby Parkinson (shoulder) questionable for Sunday's road matchup with the Eagles, Davis Allen, Tyler Higbee and rookie second-round pick Max Klare are the current healthy TEs on L.A.'s active roster.

items.headline: The Rams placed Rivers (calf) on their injured reserve list Wednesday.
items.summary: Per Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site, coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Rivers' calf injury is expected to keep him sidelined for 4-to-6 weeks. McVay also said the team plans to elevate either undrafted rookie Dean Connors or Jordan Waters from its practice squad for Sunday's game at Denver.

items.headline: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: With Caleb Douglas (ankle) already ruled out for Miami, Bell appears set to remain a big part of the passing offense after he set season highs in snaps, routes and targets last Sunday against Kansas City. In Miami's offense that struggles to score points coupled with Minnesota's strong defense, Bell is difficult to trust for fantasy lineups.

items.headline: Coleman played 27 offensive snaps and saw no targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: Coleman played 46 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps in the blowout loss. The fifth-round rookie appears to have taken a back seat to Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas (ankle) and Chris Bell. Coleman could see an uptick in usage in the team's Week 3 game against the Chiefs if Douglas cannot play due to his ankle injury.

items.headline: Cook (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Dolphins' emergency third quarterback against the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: As the emergency third quarterback, Cook is now allowed to play Sunday unless both Malik Willis and Kyle McCord leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Dulcich played 20 offensive snaps but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Dolphins' 15-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Dulcich and Malik Willis connected on five catches on seven targets for 55 yards against the Chiefs in Week 3, but the duo failed to link up with each other during Sunday's loss. It was the first time since Week 8 of the 2025 season that Dulcich failed to record a target, and perhaps more notably, his 20 offensive snaps were behind rookie third-round tight end Will Kacmarek's 24. The Dolphins will head back to Miami to host the Bengals for Week 5.

items.headline: Miller (hip/back) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
items.summary: Miller was questionable ahead of the meeting with Kansas City due to hip and back injuries. However, the wideout is good to go. With Caleb Douglas (ankle) ruled out, Miller, who had a touchdown in Week 2 against the 49ers, could be more involved.

items.headline: Washington caught all five of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: The third-year wideout led the Dolphins in catches, yards and targets, but he didn't have much competition as Malik Willis attempted only 17 passes in total. Washington is still looking for his first TD of 2026, but he's become Willis' top downfield option, posting a 17-219-0 line on 28 targets through four games. Washington will try to build on this effort in a Week 5 home clash with the Bengals.

items.headline: Wright rushed five times for seven yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: Wright actually started ahead of Ollie Gordon, but Gordon ended up out-snapping Wright 22 to 12 and turned his nine carries into 100 yards and a touchdown. Gordon also saw two targets to Wright's zero. Wright figures to see a handful of carries each week alongside Gordon, but the latter is the preferred back for fantasy.

items.headline: The Dolphins signed Henning to the practice squad Thursday.
items.summary: Henning was waived by Miami on Aug. 31 but will now find himself back on the practice squad. While he is not on the active roster currently, that may change ahead of the Week 3 meeting with the Chiefs if Caleb Douglas (ankle), Ryan Miller (hip) and/or Chris Bell (knee) aren't available.

items.headline: Addison caught four of six targets for 52 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins. He added minus-1 yard on his only carry.
items.summary: With Justin Jefferson (ankle) out of commission, Addison was expected to step up as Kyler Murray's top downfield option. Instead, it was tight end T.J. Hockenson who emerged as the veteran QB's favorite target, posting a 13-119-0 line. Jefferson may not be sidelined for long, and with Hockenson now building chemistry with Murray, there may not be much volume left over for Addison in a lackluster passing attack. He'll look to make a bigger impact in a Week 5 road trip to New Orleans.

items.headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Vikings' emergency third quarterback against the Dolphins on Sunday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Brosmer was signed to the 53-man roster Tuesday after the Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy to the Giants a day earlier. As the emergency third quarterback, Brosmer is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Claiborne carried the ball three times for 12 yards during Minnesota's win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: Claiborne continued to serve a limited role behind Aaron Jones even with Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. Claiborne will look to be more involved offensively during next week's matchup versus the Saints.

items.headline: Dallas (toe) practiced fully Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Tampa Bay.
items.summary: Dallas kicked off Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a toe injury, but his ability to handle every on-field rep Friday clears him to be available to the Vikings backfield this weekend. With Aaron Jones (knee) also gaining clearance to play Sunday, Dallas likely will remain relegated to a small workload, as the latter has just four touches on his 14 offensive snaps through two games on the campaign.

items.headline: Hockenson caught all 13 of his targets for 119 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
items.summary: The veteran tight end emerged as Kyler Murray's favorite target in the absence of Justin Jefferson (ankle), and as a result Hockenson produced his first game with 100-plus yards since 2024, when he popped for a 7-114-0 line against the Bears in Week 12. Hockenson came into Sunday with just 76 receiving yards, so he could have trouble repeating the performance even if Jefferson misses another game, but Murray had success feeding the ball to Trey McBride last year with Arizona as well -- McBride posted a 29-275-1 line on 42 targets during the five games they were in the lineup together. Hockenson will look to keep rolling in a Week 5 road trip to New Orleans.

items.headline: Jennings caught his lone target for eight yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
items.summary: Despite Justin Jefferson (ankle) missing Sunday's game, Jennings remained a non-factor on offense, as he took a distant back seat to all three of T.J. Hockenson, Jordan Addison and Aaron Jones. Jennings has two catches for nine yards on four targets across 152 offensive snaps through three games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.
