items.headline: The Vikings placed Oliver (biceps) on injured reserve Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Oliver's move to IR was expected after the tight end was diagnosed with a torn bicep Monday. The tight end will likely miss most, if not all, of the 2026 season as he recovers from surgery. T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are now the only tight ends on the Vikings' roster, meaning practice-squad elevations ahead of Week 4 will likely include at least one more option at the position. The Vikings signed linebacker Kyle Van Noy to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Estime to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Estime worked out for the team Tuesday and will provide backfield depth behind Aaron Jones, Demond Claiborne and special-teamer DeeJay Dallas while Jordan Mason (thumb) remains on injured reserve for at least the next two games. Estime has handled 122 career regular-season carries for 508 yards and three touchdowns.

items.headline: Neal (hamstring) signed a contract with the Vikings' practice squad Wednesday, Rob Kleifield of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: New Orleans waived Neal in early September on an injury settlement while the second-year running back tended to a hamstring issue, but he appears to have since made a full recovery. After working out with Minnesota on Tuesday, Neal quickly landed a contract, improving the organization's depth at running back while Jordan Mason (thumb) is on injured reserve. As a rookie last season, Neal appeared in 10 games for the Saints, carrying 57 times for 206 yards (3.6 average) and two touchdowns while adding 17 receptions for 104 yards on 19 targets.

items.headline: Douglas caught two of three targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 29-26 win over Buffalo.
items.summary: Douglas didn't really make much of a splash in Week 4, but he was able to reel in multiple passes for the first time since Week 1. The wide receiver could step into a more prominent role beginning in Week 5 against the Raiders after Mack Hollins suffered a calf injury in Sunday's victory. Through four contests this season, Douglas has caught nine of 17 targets for 82 yards.

items.headline: Henderson rushed 14 times for 42 yards and failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: Henderson struggled to get anything going against an improved Bills run defense, averaging an even 3.0 yards per carry. The second-year pro logged one more carry than backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson but finished with five fewer rushing yards, and through three games, Henderson is averaging a pedestrian 3.7 yards per tote while only adding one catch for six yards. The 2025 second-round pick's next opportunity for his first breakout effort of 2026 comes in a Week 5 home matchup against a vastly improved Raiders team.

items.headline: Henry finished with five receptions for 62 yards on five targets in Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills.
items.summary: The catch and yardage totals were season-best marks for Henry, who took the field for 49 of the Patriots' 76 offensive snaps (64.5 percent). With fellow tight end Eli Raridon (ankle) making an early exit from the contest and potentially at risk of missing the Patriots' Week 5 game against the Raiders, Henry could be called upon to handle a heftier workload next Sunday.

items.headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said that he expects to know more about Hollins' calf injury later Monday, and the Patriots are uncertain if the wideout will be able to practice "for a couple days," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.
items.summary: Hollins recorded three catches for 53 yards on four targets before exiting in the third quarter of Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills due to the calf issue. The Patriots listed Hollins as questionable to return at the time of his departure, but he never ended up checking back into the contest. More information on the severity of Hollins' injury should be known in the next day or two, but if he ends up being unavailable for next Sunday's game against the Raiders, more reps would be opened up for Efton Chism, who helped fill in for Hollins in the fourth quarter and made an acrobatic 23-yard touchdown grab with just under two minutes remaining to seal the win over Buffalo.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: As such, the rookie seventh-rounder is not allowed to play unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Raridon (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Buffalo.
items.summary: Raridon didn't play in Week 3 against the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury. However, an ankle injury could mean he won't be back in Week 4. If Raridon can't return, Cameron Latu could see more work behind Hunter Henry.

items.headline: Williams caught one of two targets for 10 yards in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
items.summary: Despite A.J. Brown (ankle) missing his first game after going down in Week 1 against Seattle, Williams played just 20 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Pittsburgh. He operated as the fourth receiver, well behind Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs and slot man DeMario Douglas. Williams doesn't hold much fantasy value in redraft formats.

items.headline: Brown was spotted Monday in the Patriots' locker room walking without a limp and wearing a small wrap on his injured right ankle, Taylor Kyles of CLNSMedia.com reports.
items.summary: Kyles noted that Brown was wearing cleats, which could hint that he was able to do some on-field exercises. After being placed on injured reserve Sept. 12, Brown won't be eligible to start practicing with his teammates until Week 6, but the wideout at least seems to be making good progress in his recovery from the high-ankle sprain he sustained in the season-opening loss to the Seahawks.

items.headline: The Patriots signed Conner to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The addition of Conner gives the Patriots depth at tight end, and he would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster for the Patriots' Week 3 game against the Jaguars if rookie third-rounder Eli Raridon (thigh) cannot play. Tanner appeared in nine regular-season games for the Dolphins in 2025, logging nine catches (on 15 targets) for 91 yards while also contributing on special teams.

items.headline: The Saints signed Austin from their practice squad to their active roster Thursday.
items.summary: Austin was elevated from the practice squad each of the first three weeks, so this signing was necessary for him to continue to be part of New Orleans' gameday roster. The Notre Dame product hasn't been a big part of the team's offense, however, logging just 20 offensive snaps across three contests and catching his only target for seven yards. Austin should continue to work in a depth wideout role behind Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance.

items.headline: Brown (hamstring) has no injury designation ahead of Monday's Week 4 matchup against Atlanta.
items.summary: Brown missed last Sunday's loss to Las Vegas due to a hamstring injury. However, he logged an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week and has been cleared to suit up Monday. Brown's primary role for the Saints this season has been as a kick and punt returner, and he has no targets on offense so far while logging nine offensive snaps through two games.

items.headline: Delp gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 24-17 victory over the Ravens.
items.summary: Delp didn't suit up for the 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit in Week 1 due to a hamstring issue, though he was on the field for Sunday's 24-17 upset win over Baltimore. However, despite the rookie's availability in Week 2, he appeared in just nine of the Saints' 68 offensive snaps, catching his only target for eight yards, while logging six snaps on special teams. Although Delp could see more action moving ahead, it doesn't appear as if he will be more involved than Noah Fant and Juwan Johnson anytime soon.

items.headline: Fant (abdomen) is listed as inactive for Monday's game against the Falcons.
items.summary: Despite being a limited practice participant during Week 4 prep, Fant will miss his first contest of the campaign due to an abdominal injury. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch thus will serve as the reserve tight ends behind starter Juwan Johnson on Monday. Fant's next chance to play is this coming Sunday versus the Vikings.

items.headline: Johnson secured six of eight targets for 59 yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
items.summary: Johnson tied for second in receptions and also finished as the runner-up in receiving yards on the night for the Saints in the lopsided loss. The veteran tight end has gotten the season off to a productive start, recording at least 53 receiving yards in each contest and posting 14 of his 21 catches of the season in the last two games alone. Johnson also has drawn at least seven targets in three of the first four games, affording him a very appealing fantasy floor going into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

items.headline: Lance caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 24-17 victory against Baltimore.
items.summary: Lance was on the field for 54 of New Orleans' 68 offensive snaps, but he had only one pass thrown his way by Tyler Shough. Chris Olave (10 targets) and Devaughn Vele (seven) got 17 of the Saints' 19 total wideout targets, so Lance wasn't alone in having a quiet day among the team's complementary options. Barion Brown logged just two offensive snaps Sunday and Kevin Austin notched five, so Lance seems to be clearly ahead of both in the pecking order.

items.headline: Miller is in line for a larger offensive role for as long as Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on injured reserve, John DeShazler of the Saints' official site reports.
items.summary: Etienne's placement on IR on Thursday comes after the star running back aggravated a hamstring injury during the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. With Etienne sidelined, Miller and Alvin Kamara figure to operate as the Saints' top running backs moving forward, with undrafted rookie CJ Donaldson also in the mix for backfield work. Miller has 13 carries for 44 yards (3.4 YPC) and a touchdown along with two catches (on three targets) for five yards through two regular-season games.

items.headline: Moreno-Cooper reverted to New Orleans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction report.
items.summary: Moreno-Cooper was elevated to provide additional depth at receiver as Barion Brown (hamstring) was inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders. Moreno-Cooper ended up playing exclusively on special teams and returned one kickoff for 22 yards. The 25-year-old could be elevated again for the Week 4 matchup versus the Falcons if Brown remains sidelined.

items.headline: Shough completed 30 of 48 passes for 286 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for five yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
items.summary: Shough's final line was perfectly acceptable from a fantasy standpoint, but Monday night was a case of the numbers being much more aesthetically pleasing than the on-field results. He piled up a significant part of his production in the second half -- including a three-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele with 1:13 remaining -- after the Saints already faced a sizable deficit, as he led a couple of 13-play drives in the fourth quarter when New Orleans was down by 21 and 28 points, respectively. Nevertheless, Shough generated his second interception-free performance of the last three games, and he's up to 1,203 passing yards and a 9:3 TD:INT along with 72 rushing yards and another score heading into a Week 5 home matchup against an aggressive Vikings defense on Sunday.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback for Monday night's contest against the Falcons.
items.summary: Wilson will operate as the team's No. 3 QB for the fourth game in a row to begin the 2026 campaign. Wilson will only be eligible to enter the contest if both starter Tyler Shough and top backup Spencer Rattler are forced out of the game.

items.headline: The Saints signed Bentley to their practice squad Thursday.
items.summary: Bentley spent all of last season with Indianapolis and was with the Colts in training camp this year. He was cut from the team's practice squad in early September and has now gotten a new opportunity with New Orleans. The Saints became in need of backfield depth when Travis Etienne (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Thursday.

items.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed Berrios is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, but a decision has yet to be made regarding whether the wideout will be placed on injured reserve, Paul Schwartz of the New York Post reports.
items.summary: Though Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that Berrios was ticketed for IR, the Giants apparently plan to evaluate the 30-year-old over the next few days before deciding whether or not to deactivate him. Regardless, Berrios appears poised to miss time, which would pave the way for Charlie Jones to replace him as the Giants' primary return man beginning with Sunday's game against the Commanders. Berrios has suited up for each of the Giants' first four games, drawing just one target while seeing the majority of his playing time on special teams.

items.headline: Fidone (coach's decision) is inactive against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: The 2025 seventh-rounder has been a healthy scratch for each of the Giants' first four games of the regular season, and his next opportunity to play is Week 5 against the Commanders on Sunday, Oct. 11. The Giants will go with Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson and Chris Manhertz as the active tight ends for Sunday's game.

items.headline: Fields caught two of three targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Fields has emerged as the Giants' clear WR3 in terms of routes, as he ran 22 routes to Malik Nabers' 30 and Darnell Mooney's 26 against Arizona. On the season, Fields has out-targeted Mooney 15 to 10. Fields caught a 12-yard score from Jameis Winston on Sunday, and now has eight catches for 126 yards and the one score through four contests to begin his rookie season.

items.headline: Haener reverted to the Giants' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Haener was active for Sunday's 36-24 win versus the Cardinals, but his services were not needed, as veteran journeyman Jameis Winston started and finished the game at quarterback. Whether Haener is called up again in Week 5 might depend on how quickly recent trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy is able to familiarize himself with his new playbook.

items.headline: Harris logged nine carries for 30 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 36-24 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Harris saw half the carries of Cam Skattebo as the Giants' primary relief option in Sunday's contest. The running back coughed up the football to Mack Wilson on the Cardinals' 42-yard line in the fourth quarter when the score was 27-24 Giants. The Giants' defense held strong to close out the contest despite Harris' mistake.

items.headline: The Giants signed Jones to the active roster from their practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Jones will slot in as the team's fifth-string receiver following the release of Odell Beckham earlier in the day. Jones is also expected to serve as the backup punt returner behind Braxton Berrios.

items.headline: Likely caught seven of 12 targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 36-24 win over Arizona.
items.summary: The targets and catches led the Giants on the day, but Likely's yardage total was well behind Malik Nabers' 112. Likely has remained an important part of the passing game with Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), and in Winston's three appearances (two starts) the tight end has delivered a 14-112-0 line on 27 targets, seeing double-digit looks twice. Likely will look to find the end zone for the first time since the season opener in a Week 5 road clash with the Commanders.

items.headline: Mooney caught two passes on three targets for 20 yards and logged a nine-yard carry during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.summary: Mooney has logged two catches in each of the first three games of the season, and his 95 receiving yards are third-most on the Giants behind tight end Isaiah Likely (124) and Malik Nabers (96). The Giants will stay home in Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up the second-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season.

items.headline: Singletary (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Singletary will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive week while the Giants roll with Tyrone Tracy and Najee Harris as the backup options in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo. Singletary's next opportunity to suit up is Week 5 against the Commanders on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Tracy (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Tracy upgraded his practice participation level in each of the Giants' Week 4 prep sessions. The running back went from a DNP on Wednesday to limited Thursday before finally achieving full participation Friday, in time to avoid an injury designation. Tracy is set to suit up for Sunday's game as the No. 3 option behind Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris.

items.headline: Allen rushed 14 times for 59 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Allen accounted for all 14 of the Jets' rushing attempts in the absence of Breece Hall (quadriceps), who is considered week-to-week. The Bears dominated time of possession as Geno Smith completed just eight passes in the loss. If Hall isn't ready to return in Week 5 against the Browns, Allen would retain the lead role in the backfield for the Jets.

items.headline: Davis played just two offensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Bears.
items.summary: With Breece Hall (thigh) inactive, Braelon Allen ended up playing 32 of 34 offensive snaps out of the backfield for the Jets, leaving no room for Davis. He can continue to be ignored in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: The Jets signed McClain from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: The Jets needed depth at wide receiver due to Omar Cooper (ankle), Tim Patrick (groin) and, most recently, Arian Smith (knee) going on injured reserve. The Jets now have four healthy wide receivers on the active roster in McClain, Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams. McClain joined the Jets in early May as an undrafted free agent following his final college season at Arizona State, when he caught 31 passes for 441 yards and one touchdown across 13 games.

items.headline: Nwangwu (back) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: Head coach Aaron Glenn suggested before Wednesday's session that Nwangwu would be limited in practice, but the running back instead took every rep in the Jets' first Week 4 session. With the back issue seemingly behind him, Nwangwu looks ready to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Bears. Lead back Breece Hall (quadriceps) is considered week-to-week and will likely sit out Sunday, leaving Nwangwu in line to serve as the Jets' No. 3 back behind Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis.

items.headline: The Jets signed Pritchett from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: The Jets signed Pritchett to the practice squad Sept. 2 after waiving the wide receiver on cutdown day. The second-year player out of South Alabama has yet to play in an NFL contest. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) cannot suit up for Sunday's game against the Lions, Pritchett is set to be the No. 4 option for the Jets in his debut.

items.headline: Ruckert (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
items.summary: Ruckert was limited Wednesday and Thursday but managed to log a full session Friday, clearing the way for his availability for the Week 4 meeting with the Bears. With Mason Taylor (thumb) still sidelined, Ruckert should continue to be more involved. He might see the field even more Sunday if Kenyon Sadiq (back), who is questionable, can't suit up.

items.headline: Wilson caught three of four targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Wilson accounted for two of Geno Smith's three completions in the first half, and the star wide receiver finished with a team-high three catches as Smith completed only eight passes in a forgettable performance from New York's offense. Heading into Sunday's loss, Wilson had been averaging seven catches for 81 receiving yards per game. Wilson and the Jets will try to bounce back from this dud in Week 5 against the Browns.

items.headline: Smith (knee) underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn ACL and will miss the rest of the season, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
items.summary: Smith suffered a knee injury during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He will finish the 2026 campaign without a catch (one target), adding four carries for 13 yards. With Smith, Omar Cooper (ankle) and Tim Patrick (groin) out of the equation, Isaiah Williams could be in line for more opportunities behind Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson. The Jets also signed Malik McClain off the practice squad Tuesday, which will help fill some of the void left by the injuries within the receiving corps.

items.headline: The Jets signed Hardy to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Hardy failed to make the Saints' active roster after training camp, but he'll get a new opportunity with the Jets on the practice squad. Mason Taylor (thumb) is considered doubtful for Week 3 against the Lions, so Hardy is a candidate to be elevated to the active roster for that contest to provide depth at tight end.

items.headline: Brown (ankle) is listed as out ahead of Sunday's game against the Rams.
items.summary: Brown didn't practice all week and will now miss his second game of the 2026 campaign. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) ruled out, Brown could have had an enhanced role if he was cleared to play in Week 4. However, with Brown, Smith and Dallas Goedert (knee) all on the shelf, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will likely serve as Jalen Hurts' primary receiving options.

items.headline: Dalton is expected to serve as the Eagles' No. 3 quarterback for Sunday's game against the Rams, while Tanner McKee moves up to second on the depth chart as the top backup to Jalen Hurts, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Dalton had been active ahead of McKee as the No. 2 quarterback for each of the Eagles' first three games of the season, but he didn't see any action until midway through the second quarter of Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears, when Hurts exited to get checked for a concussion. After three consecutive handoffs to Saquon Barkley got the Eagles to two-yard line to set up a third-and-goal, Dalton proceeded to throw a back-breaking interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt before Hurts returned for the ensuing possession. The costly pick looks to have been enough to cost Dalton the No. 2 job, at least for one week.

items.headline: Deguara reverted to the practice squad with Philadelphia on Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Deguara was elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams, and he did not log a snap on offense in the contest. The 29-year-old was on the field for 21 snaps with the special-teams unit, failing to record any stats during the game. Deguara can be elevated two more times before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

items.headline: Lemon caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Lemon had a chance to step into a more prominent role on offense in the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), but he didn't really see an increase in production. The wide receiver's six targets were a new career high, but he has now registered three or fewer catches in all four games this season while never exceeding 30 receiving yards. Quarterback Jalen Hurts recorded only 93 total passing yards Sunday, so he'll have to better for Lemon to see an increase in production Week 5 versus Jacksonville.

items.headline: McKee is expected to be active for Sunday's game against the Rams as the top backup to starter Jalen Hurts, while Andy Dalton serves as the Eagles' No. 3 quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Despite operating as Hurts' primary backup in 2025, McKee slid to third on the depth chart entering the 2026 season after the Eagles acquired Dalton in a trade with the Panthers back in March. Dalton didn't see any snaps on the season until midway through the second quarter of Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears, when Hurts made a brief exit from the contest to get checked for a concussion. After three consecutive Saquon Barkley carries got the Eagles near the goal line, Dalton proceeded to throw a costly interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt before Hurts returned for the next possession. The gaffe appears to have resulted in Dalton turning the backup gig over to McKee, at least for one week.

items.headline: Mundt caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-20 win against the Titans.
items.summary: Mundt started along with fellow tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and he logged 49 of Philadelphia's 76 offensive snaps. The significant playing time was partly due to Goedert exiting in the first half after spraining his MCL. Goedert is now slated to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, but that won't necessarily mean that Mundt will be an attractive fantasy waiver-wire pickup. The Eagles signed veteran Zach Ertz to a contract Tuesday, and he'll likely slide in as the team's top tight end during Goedert's absence, though it's unclear how long Ertz will need to get up to speed.

items.headline: Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams. He also returned three kickoffs for 65 yards.
items.summary: Shipley was the last man standing in Philadelphia's backfield after Saquon Barkley (hamstring) exited in the first quarter and Tank Bigsby (undisclosed) left in the fourth quarter. Bigsby had been working ahead of Shipley after Barkley's exit, but if neither of Philadelphia's top two running backs are available in Week 5, Shipley could take on the lead role against the Jaguars in London.

items.headline: Allar (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Cleveland, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are active for the AFC North showdown with the Browns, and Will Howard (coach's decision) will serve as the emergency quarterback. As a result, Allar will be a healthy scratch for the fourth consecutive week.

items.headline: Bernard caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
items.summary: Bernard was not targeted by Aaron Rodgers until late in the fourth quarter, with the duo connecting on passes for six and five yards to help set up a three-yard touchdown catch by Pat Freiermuth after the two-minute warning. The rookie second-rounder was on the field for 29 of the Steelers' 72 offensive snaps (40.3 percent), which was third most among wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (70) and Michael Pittman (52) and ahead of Roman Wilson (22). Bernard has a 7-60-0 line on 11 targets through four regular-season games, though his role in the offense will be limited behind Metcalf, Pittman, Freiermuth, Darnell Washington and Jaylen Warren. The Steelers head back home for Week 5 against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Head coach Mike McCarthy said that Dowdle (toe) had a positive workout Friday and is "making progress" in his recovery, but the Steelers aren't yet certain if he'll be available to play Week 5 versus the Colts, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
items.summary: Dowdle's right toe injury has kept him out for the past two games, with his consecutive absences enabling Jaylen Warren to take on a heightened role out of the backfield as Pittsburgh's clear top option. Though Warren has ran efficiently (6.5 yards per carry) on heavy volume (34 totes) while chipping in six receptions for 82 yards over the last two weeks, McCarthy emphasized that Dowdle will likely remain part of a "one-two punch" with Warren once he returns. Before sustaining the injury in Week 2, Dowdle had struggled to find open running room, taking his 15 carries for just 37 yards (2.5 average).

items.headline: Freiermuth brought in three of five targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
items.summary: Freiermuth and fellow tight end Darnell Washington each had three catches and a touchdown on five targets, as the two continued in a pretty even timeshare at the position. Freiermuth's scoring grab was particularly timely, as it came with 1:42 remaining and put the Steelers within two points of knotting the game up at 24-24. Freiermuth has multiple receptions in every game this season and a pair of touchdown catches, and he should remain in a similar role when Pittsburgh returns to action in a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Heidenreich (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
items.summary: It looked like the rookie seventh-rounder was in line for a slightly larger role Sunday after Rico Dowdle (toe) was ruled out. However, Heidenreich will be a healthy scratch for the first time this season, with Travis Homer and Lew Nichols providing depth in the backfield for Jaylen Warren while fellow rookie Kaden Wetjen operates as the primary returner on kickoffs. Heidenreich's next chance to play is Thursday against the Browns.

items.headline: Homer posted two carries for minus-1 yard during Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
items.summary: With Rico Dowdle (toe) out for a second consecutive contest, Homer had an opportunity for more involvement. However, the 2019 No. 204 overall pick didn't do much of relevance, logging just two of the Steelers' 72 offensive snaps to finish well behind Jaylen Warren (70). Even if Dowdle misses more time moving forward, it's hard to imagine Homer doing anything to benefit fantasy managers if Warren is active.

items.headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Cleveland. However, he is listed as the Steelers' emergency quarterback, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph occupy the top two spots on the depth chart, though if both of those players exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection, Howard will see the field as the emergency signal-caller.

items.headline: Metcalf brought in five of nine targets for 115 yards in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
items.summary: Metcalf led the Steelers across the stat sheet in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his production in the first two categories also qualified as new season highs. The veteran wideout started slowly, but he came on with catches of 43, 22 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. The standout night was a welcome sight for fantasy managers, who'd seen Metcalf post an inefficient and modest 11-98-1 line on 24 targets over his first three games. Metcalf will aim to carry over the momentum into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Nichols reverted to the Steelers' practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Nichols played nine special-teams snaps Thursday in his second elevation to the active roster in 2026. The running back saw zero offensive snaps and did not appear in the box score. Nichols has one remaining elevation before the Steelers will need to sign the 25-year-old to the active roster for him to appear in any more regular-season games.

items.headline: Pittman caught two of four targets for 15 yards Thursday in a loss to the Browns.
items.summary: Pittman logged a 72 percent offensive snap share, second-most among Pittsburgh wideouts, but he didn't do much with the ample playing time. In fact, Roman Wilson -- who logged a 22 percent offensive snap share -- outproduced Pittman considerably with a 3-74-1 receiving line. In his first season with the Steelers, Pittman has had a tough time connecting with QB Aaron Rodgers, posting just seven catches on 12 targets for 89 yards through three games. He'll look to make more of an impact in Week 5 against Indianapolis next Sunday.

items.headline: Skowronek hauled in his lone target for a 23-yard touchdown during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.summary: Skowronek ranked fifth among Steelers receivers by playing 11 of the team's 62 offensive snaps, but the 29-year-old was able to connect with quarterback Aaron Rodgers on a pass to the end zone during his limited time on the field. Despite coming up with a big play in the Week 3 win, Skowronek remains likely to see most of his field time on special teams moving forward.

items.headline: Wilson brought in three of six targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
items.summary: Wilson capped off a marathon 17-play opening drive for the Steelers by showcasing his speed, as the second-year wideout scored from 12 yards out on a shovel pass from Aaron Rodgers. Wilson has at least three catches in each of his first four games, and Thursday's yardage total established a new season high after he'd also done so with his 60-yard tally in Week 3. Wilson also has exactly six targets in each contest thus far, cementing him as a key complementary component of the air attack heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: The Steelers signed Hodgins to the practice squad Tuesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Giants cut Hodgins on Aug. 29, and he's been on the hunt for a new team since. Hodgins will now provide organizational depth to a Steelers offense that may be without Michael Pittman (foot) for the team's Week 3 divisional matchup with the Bengals. Hodgins played seven regular-season games for the Giants in 2025, catching 10 passes for 115 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Black turned six carries into 13 yards during the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
items.summary: Black's longest carry of the day went for five yards, with four of his other touches going for two yards or fewer. With Christian McCaffrey clearly leading the backfield, Black's workload will be volatile on a week-to-week basis and dependant on game script. The 49ers will hit the road for Week 5 in an NFC West showdown against the 3-1 Seahawks.

items.headline: Cowing failed to corral either of his two targets while playing 17 of the 49ers' 54 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Even though Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was moved to injured reserve following Week 2 and Mike Evans (rib) was unable to finish Sunday's contest, Cowing didn't benefit from much of a spike in playing time. In fact, after logging 24 of the 49ers' 52 offensive snaps (46.2 percent) in Week 2, Cowing saw his snap share drop to 31.5 percent. The biggest beneficiary of Robinson's absence and Evans' early exit was KhaDarel Hodge, who finished second to only Deebo Samuel (39) among 49ers receivers with 30 snaps.

items.headline: James (coach's decision) is inactive against Denver on Sunday.
items.summary: The second-year pro will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines while the 49ers roll with two active running backs in Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. James' next chance to play is Week 5 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 11.

items.headline: Jones did not attempt a pass and lost two yards on two end-of-game kneel-down plays during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Dolphins.
items.summary: The 49ers had no trouble building a comfortable lead throughout the contest, leading to Jones coming in to mop up over the final two series. The 28-year-old is coming off a sound 2025 campaign, throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions while completing a career-best 69.6 percent of his attempts. While Jones is considered one of the better backup quarterbacks in the NFL, his fantasy ceiling is virtually non-existent as long as Brock Purdy is healthy.

items.headline: McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 52 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 18 yards in the 49ers' 24-14 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
items.summary: McCaffrey saw a reduced workload by his lofty standards, although he still outpaced backfield mate Kaelon Black by nine carries. The star back had to tough out the majority of his gains on the ground, including his one-yard touchdown run with just under nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. McCaffrey has yet to top 15 carries in any game this season, but he has four rushing TDs and 340 total yards heading into a Week 5 road showdown against the Seahawks next Sunday.

items.headline: Turner reverted to the 49ers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Turner played 17 snaps on special teams in the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. The wide receiver took over gunner duties for KhaDarel Hodge (knee), who was waived from the team's IR last Thursday. Turner did not appear in the box score during his first game of the 2026 regular season.

items.headline: Watkins recorded two receptions for 60 yards on two targets in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Making his 2026 debut after he was a healthy inactive for the 49ers' first two contests, Watkins took the field for 15 of the team's 54 offensive snaps and was able to make a mark with 34- and 26-yard grabs. He still finished fifth among 49ers receivers in playing time, but he could see an uptick in opportunities if the rib strain Mike Evans suffered Sunday prevents him from playing Week 4 against the Broncos.

items.headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers could open Kirk's (calf) practice window to return from injured reserve in two weeks, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Shanahan reiterated that Kirk is unlikely to be back at practice next week but is aiming to start participating in sessions following the 49ers' Week 5 tilt against the Seahawks. Kirk opened the season on injured reserve due to a calf injury he sustained in training camp in late July. The 49ers' WR room has been decimated by injuries, with Kirk, Demarcus Robinson (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee) and rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all on IR, and veteran Mike Evans injured his ribs during a Week 3 win over the Cardinals. Given the timeline Shanahan provided, it seems Kirk could be available as soon as Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19.

items.headline: The 49ers placed Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Robinson was carted off the field due to a right ankle injury during San Francisco's Week 2 win against the Dolphins, after which coach Kyle Shanahan relayed that the wide receiver likely suffered a high-ankle sprain. On Monday, Shanahan said that Robinson was facing a recovery timeline of 3-to-6 weeks, so this move to injured reserve doesn't come as a surprise. Robinson will be first eligible to return to action Sunday, Oct. 25 in Atlanta, but with all of Christian Kirk (calf), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee) and Robinson on IR, the 49ers will be going with Mike Evans (hip), Deebo Samuel, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge at wide receiver this Sunday against the Cardinals.

items.headline: San Francisco signed Pettis to its practice squad Tuesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.summary: The 49ers must have liked what they saw when they worked out Pettis on Tuesday, as he's now already a member of their practice squad. The team is dealing with injuries to more than a few of its wide receivers, including veterans Mike Evans (ribs) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle), so Pettis could see himself elevated to the active roster relatively soon.

items.headline: Arroyo didn't record any catches during Seattle's win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.summary: Arroyo wasn't targeted once for the third time this season across four outings. The 2025 second-round pick will likely continue to see minimal offensive output as the team's third-string tight end behind AJ Barner and Eric Saubert.

items.headline: Barner caught one of three targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
items.summary: Barner wasn't particularly busy in Week 4, garnering three or fewer targets for the third time this season. The tight end remains an unappealing fantasy option as the Seahawks' passing attack funnels through Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the rest of Seattle's pass-catchers are just reaching for crumbs.

items.headline: Foster (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Commanders.
items.summary: Foster will be inactive for the second consecutive week. His next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 4 versus the Chargers.

items.headline: Holani rushed seven times for 18 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers. He added one catch for two yards on one target.
items.summary: Even with Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve, Holani played a distant second fiddle to Emanuel Wilson, who rushed 21 times for 81 yards and a touchdown. Wilson also turned four targets into three catches for 30 yards and a second score. Holani has minimal fantasy value, especially with Zach Charbonnet (knee) due back in the near future.

items.headline: Horton brought in his lone target for a six-yard touchdown during Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
items.summary: Horton saw just one target from Sam Darnold in Sunday's game, but the second-year wideout answered the call by hauling in the pass for a six-yard touchdown early in the third quarter to extend Seattle's lead to 27-6. It was Horton's fifth touchdown catch of his young NFL career and first since his two-TD performance in Week 9 of the 2025 season, which was the last game of his rookie campaign due to shin and groin injuries. Horton is firmly entrenched as the Seahawks' WR4 on the roster behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp, and Horton is also behind Shaheed as a returner on kickoffs and punts.

items.headline: Seattle signed Jones from the practice squad to the 53-man roster Saturday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Seahawks needed running-back depth ahead of Sunday's matchup versus the Chargers after rookie Jadarian Price (chest) was placed on IR. Jones should slide into the team's No. 3 RB role behind Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Jones was previously elevated from the practice squad twice this season and has logged 39 snaps, all on special teams.

items.headline: Kupp caught one of two targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Chargers.
items.summary: Kupp played 34 of 60 offensive snaps and ran 17 routes on Sam Darnold's 26 dropbacks. The veteran wide receiver has failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of the first four games, totaling nine grabs for 114 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets. He's well off the fantasy radar with Jaxon Smith-Njigba dominating the looks in Seattle.

items.headline: Lock will return to a backup role for Sunday's game at Washington after coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Sam Darnold (glute) is "going to play," John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.summary: After Darnold suffered a right glute injury on Seattle's first possession of the season Week 1 against the Patriots, Lock directed the offense for the next seven-plus quarters, leading the team to two victories while completing 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing twice for 13 yards. With Darnold back in action this weekend, though, Lock's time as the starter is over for now.

items.headline: Milroe (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Chargers on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.summary: Because Milroe is the emergency QB3, the second-year pro is now allowed to play Sunday unless both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Charbonnet (knee) won't be activated from the reserve/PUP list in advance of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports.
items.summary: Seattle opened Charbonnet's 21-day practice window last Thursday, with the running back practicing on a limited basis for the team's final two sessions of Week 4 in what amounted to his first involvement in on-field drills since he tore the ACL in his left knee Jan. 17. Macdonald noted that Charbonnet will take another step forward in Week 5 by getting "team reps" in practices, but the 25-year-old looks like he'll still need some additional time after that to fully ramp up before making his 2026 debut. With rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest) going on injured reserve this past Saturday, Emanuel Wilson took over as the Seahawks' lead back in the Week 4 win over the Chargers, finishing with 120 yards from scrimmage on 24 touches. Wilson will likely continue to carry the load out of the Seattle backfield until Charbonnet is activated.

items.headline: The Seahawks cut Hicks from the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The 27-year-old wide receiver has never appeared in a regular-season NFL game. He bounced on and off Seattle's roster during the summer.

items.headline: Meiga was signed to the Seahawks' practice squad Wednesday, John Boyle of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Seattle hosted Meiga for a tryout Tuesday, and he will now get a chance to prove himself with the team moving forward. The wide receiver was waived after reaching an injury settlement with Carolina on Aug. 12, but he has now fully recovered from an undisclosed injury.

items.headline: Daniels completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and rushed eight times for 55 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie was thrust into his first NFL start much sooner than expected thanks to Baker Mayfield's thumb injury, and all told, Daniels acquitted himself reasonably well. He unsurprisingly had his share of struggles as a passer, and in addition to his pair of picks, he also took three sacks. Daniels' two turnovers did lead to 10 total points for the Packers, but the Kansas product also provided plenty of valuable production on the ground and fired his first career touchdown to Kenny Gainwell from 10 yards out to open the fourth quarter. Daniels won't get the benefit of another full week of practice before taking the field for his second start, however, as the Bucs pay a visit to the Cowboys for a Week 5 matchup Thursday night.

items.headline: Egbuka brought in two of four targets for 13 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Egbuka's production downturn was at least partly the result of Jalon Daniels' up-and-down NFL debut under center. The second-year wideout was third in targets and tied for third in receptions with multiple teammates on the afternoon, but Egbuka's yardage total, which was a season low, bested only that of Kameron Johnson's (three yards) in the loss. Egbuka now has a 15-154-1 line on 24 targets over his first four games, and with Baker Mayfield (thumb) reportedly in line to miss up to a total of seven weeks, the former will have to progressively build chemistry with Daniels to retain solid fantasy value.

items.headline: Godwin brought in six of seven targets for 31 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Godwin led the Buccaneers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards on the afternoon. The latter total was especially nothing to write home about, but it was the byproduct of rookie Jalon Daniels throwing for only 148 yards in his NFL debut. Godwin and the rest of the Buccaneers' air attack currently have fairly dim prospects while Daniels takes his initial lumps at the NFL level, and with Baker Mayfield (thumb) unlikely to return before November per latest reports, the veteran receiver has limited fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Hurst caught two of his three targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Hurst has now seen three targets in consecutive weeks. While the third-round rookie did not score as he did in Week 3, he doubled his receptions while garnering attention from new quarterback Jalon Daniels.

items.headline: Irving rushed 16 times for 61 yards in the Buccaneers' 17-14 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Irving was surprisingly held without a single target in the narrow loss, despite rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels being under center and the third-year running back being a highly trustworthy safety valve out of the backfield. Irving worked hard for his yards on the ground as well, with his longest run of the day going for only seven yards. Irving has yet to eclipse 89 rushing yards in any of his first four games, and with reports Baker Mayfield may be in line for close to a two-month absence due to his thumb injury, the former may have to get accustomed to running against loaded defensive fronts for the foreseeable future.

items.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 17 yards during Tampa Bay's loss versus the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Johnson hauled in a season-high two receptions during the loss but still continues to see limited playing time as the team's No. 4 receiver. It would likely take an injury to either Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin or Ted Hurst for Johnson to see a larger role offensively.

items.headline: Kieft (elbow) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
items.summary: Kieft didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to an elbow injury. With no upgrade in his practice status Friday, the 28-year-old is set to miss his first game of the season. Cade Otton and Payne Durham will continue to operate as the team's top tight ends.

items.headline: Otton caught four of six targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 17-14 loss to the Packers.
items.summary: With rookie Jalon Daniels making his first career start, he leaned on Otton in the passing game, and the tight end ended up leading the team in receiving yards despite seeing one fewer target than Chris Godwin. Otton has turned 23 targets into 15 catches for 157 yards through four games this season.

items.headline: Stick reverted to Tampa Bay's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Stick was active as Jalon Daniels' backup but didn't see the field. He'll likely be back up with the Bucs each of the next couple weeks while Bake Mayfield continues to nurse a thumb injury.

items.headline: Ayomanor caught his lone target for 22 yards in Sunday's loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: Ayomanor again out-snapped Calvin Ridley 30 to 30 against Baltimore and appears to have passed the veteran on the depth chart behind Carnell Tate and slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. It's still not a valuable role in a Tennessee offense that struggles to score points. Ayomanor would need an injury ahead of him to be a worthwhile fantasy player.

items.headline: Bellinger (illness) does not have an injury designation heading into Sunday's game against the Giants.
items.summary: Bellinger popped up on Thursday's injury report as a DNP due to an illness. He was limited in Friday's practice, but he's been given the green light to play Sunday against the team that selected him in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. Bellinger has turned two targets into one catch for seven yards through two regular-season games while serving as the Titans' TE2 behind Gunnar Helm.

items.headline: Carter (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's tilt against the Ravens.
items.summary: Carter was elevated from the practice squad for last Sunday's game against the Giants but ended up being a healthy scratch. The veteran running back then signed to the Titans' 53-man roster Tuesday, yet he's inactive on game day for a second straight week. It appears Carter is essentially insurance in case one of the four running backs ahead of him in the pecking order becomes unavailable.

items.headline: Helm hauled in his lone pass for five yards and caught a two-point conversion during the Titans' 24-18 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
items.summary: Helm didn't see a target from Cam Ward until the Titans' final offensive drive of the fourth quarter, with the duo connecting on a 5-yard pass before hooking up on a successful two-point conversion. Helm opened the 2026 regular season with four catches (on five targets) for 28 yards against the Jets in Week 1, but in the three games since, he has logged five receptions (on seven targets) for 32 yards. It's hard to hold much stock in Titans position players outside of rookie wideout Carnell Tate and veteran running back Tony Pollard. Helm and the Titans head back home for a Week 5 AFC South showdown against the Texans.

items.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Michael Penix Jr. elevating Falcons' offense
items.summary: Bijan Robinson and the rest of the Falcons offense has seen a big uptick in production with Penix under center.

items.headline: Ridley caught one pass on two targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: Ridley and the rest of the Titans pass catchers took a back seat to rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, who turned 12 of his targets from Cam Ward into nine catches for 145 yards. Ridley was on the field for 30 of Tennessee's 64 offensive snaps (46.9 percent), which was fewer than Tate (54), Wan'Dale Robinson (43) and Elic Ayomanor (40). Ridley is off to a slow start to the 2026 season, accumulating only three catches (on five targets) for 48 yards through four games. The Titans head home for Week 5 against the Texans, whose secondary was torched by CeeDee Lamb in a Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.

items.headline: Robinson caught three of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: Robinson was able to find paydirt for the second straight week, connecting with quarterback Cam Ward for a three-yard touchdown with 1:16 left in regulation. The wide receiver finished second on the team in targets behind rookie first-rounder Carnell Tate (12), and Robinson has now caught 16 of 23 targets for 123 yards and two touchdowns over the first four contests of the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Singleton turned three carries into two yards during the Titans' 24-18 loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
items.summary: Two of Singleton's three carries went for no gain, but he at least had some involvement in the offense after not recording a carry nor a target in Week 3 against the Giants. He actually had one more carry than Tyjae Spears, but Singleton was on the field for only eight of the Titans' 64 offensive snaps (12.5 percent), far less than Spears (23) and lead back Tony Pollard (34). Adam Schefter of ESPN notes that Pollard's name is one to watch ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, and both Spears and Singleton would take on larger roles if the Titans elect to trade Pollard to a team in need of a veteran running back.

items.headline: Tate caught nine of 12 targets for 145 yards in Sunday's 24-18 loss to Baltimore.
items.summary: While the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is still looking for his first career touchdown, Tate looked the part of a No. 1 wideout Sunday, as his 145 receiving yards were more than he'd produced in his first three games combined. He'll take a 22-268-0 line on 32 targets, and some real momentum, into a Week 5 home tilt against the Texans, whose secondary just got shredded by CeeDee Lamb for 17 catches, 189 yards and a TD.

items.headline: Allen turned three carries into one yard during the Commanders' 30-13 loss to the Colts on Sunday in London.
items.summary: Allen's first carry came early in the first quarter, but the rookie sixth-rounder didn't touch the ball again until the last five minutes of the fourth period. Even with Rachaad White (shoulder) inactive, Allen was on the field for only 12 of the Commanders' 64 offensive snaps (18.8 percent), which was behind both Jacory Croskey-Merritt (29) and recent addition Austin Ekeler (17). White is expected to return to practice ahead of the Commanders' Week 5 game against the Giants, and if he's cleared to return, then Allen would seemingly move down to the RB4 spot on the roster behind Croskey-Merritt, White and Ekeler.

items.headline: Bates played 22 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in Sunday's 37-20 loss to the Cowboys.
items.summary: Bates played 22 of the Commanders' 71 offensive snaps in his start. The tight end was primarily used as a blocker for the team's run game but did not steal any targets from Ben Sinnott in the effort.

items.headline: Croskey-Merritt carried the ball nine times for a season-low 15 yards and caught two of four targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: The Commanders' running game struggled to get anything going against an Indy front seven led by DeForest Buckner, especially once Marcus Mariota (knee) was replaced under center by seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, but Croskey-Merritt was able to salvage his production to some extent with a 35-yard catch and run on a screen pass in the first quarter that helped set up a field goal. His 11 touches led the Washington backfield, while Austin Ekeler saw five in his season debut and rookie Kaytron Allen got three, but that division of labor came with Rachaad White (shoulder) on the shelf. Croskey-Merritt's ability to improve on his numbers could depend on whether Jayden Daniels (elbow) can return at quarterback for Washington in a Week 5 home game against the Giants.

items.headline: Diggs caught five of nine targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: While the targets and receptions led the Commanders on the day, Diggs finished just fourth in receiving yards on the team as his longest gain went for only 10 yards. The veteran wideout's ability to deliver a big play was impacted by the loss of Marcus Mariota (knee) in the first quarter, leaving the offense in the hands of seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis. Diggs could be the No. 1 receiver again in Week 5 against the Giants if Terry McLaurin (hamstring) remains sidelined, but Diggs' ceiling could be limited if Jayden Daniels (elbow) isn't cleared to return.

items.headline: Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Monday that Lane (ankle) will miss the remainder of the season.
items.summary: Lane sustained a gruesome left ankle while returning a kickoff in Sunday's loss to the Colts in London and was eventually carted off the field. With Lane being diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated left ankle following an MRI, he'll require a season-ending surgery to address the injury. Dyami Brown took over as the Commanders' primary kick returner following Lane's injury.

items.headline: McCaffrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Colts in London.
items.summary: McCaffrey suited up for the first time all season in the Commanders' Week 3 win over the Seahawks, but his playing time was contained to special teams. Even with top wideout Terry McLaurin (hamstring) sitting out Sunday, McCaffrey won't be called upon to provide depth at receiver. Washington will go with Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Jaylin Lane as its available options at the position.

items.headline: Reynolds reverted to the Commanders' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Reynolds took two carries for four yards during Washington's 30-12 loss against the Colts in Week 4. Whether he's brought up again in Week 5 may depend on the availability of Rachaad White (shoulder).

items.headline: Sinnott (ribs) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.summary: Sinnott has no fantasy value, especially with Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) cleared to return against Indianapolis after missing the previous two contests. Sinnott has one catch for six yards on two targets across three appearances this season.

items.headline: Coach Dan Quinn said Monday that White (shoulder) "should" practice this week, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
items.summary: White sat out the entirety of Week 4 prep before being ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Colts in London as he deals with a shoulder injury. The Commanders resume practicing Wednesday, after which his activity level, if any, will become known. In three contests this season, White has 31 touches for 151 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD.

items.headline: Williams caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: With Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive, Williams finished second to Stefon Diggs in targets, but the rookie wideout wasn't able to do much with the volume as Athan Kaliakmanis ended up having to make his NFL debut in relief of Marcus Mariota (knee) at quarterback. Williams has produced a 12-124-1 line on 19 targets through his first four games, and he'll be a volatile option in Week 5 against the Giants depending on whether Jayden Daniels (elbow) and McLaurin are able to return.

items.headline: Yankoff caught his only target for 14 yards in Sunday's Week 2 loss to Dallas.
items.summary: Yankoff logged 21 of the Commanders' 71 offensive snaps, ranking third among the team's tight ends behind Ben Sinnott (48) and John Bates (22). Washington was without starter Chig Okonkwo, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Yankoff doesn't seem slated for a major role even with Okonkwo out of action, so he's currently off the radar in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Henry was signed to the Seahawks' active roster Monday, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
items.summary: Henry has spent the entirety of the 2026 campaign on the practice squad with Washington so far, but he will now get a chance with Seattle's active roster. The running back will provide the team with an additional depth option behind Emanuel Wilson and George Holani while Zach Charbonnet (knee) works his way back from the PUP list and Jadarian Price (chest) is on injured reserve. Seattle also signed veteran Joe Mixon to the practice squad Monday, so there are many moving parts for the team at running back right now.
